title: workbench: avoid doubled compact sidebar dividers
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #337503.

## Summary

- Keep the first connected tab's square, borderless leading edge when horizontal scrolling reconstructs its clipped cap. This avoids adding a second stroke beside the sidebar/editor divider.
- Snap Compact layout's painted card separators to native border thickness using the effective device-pixel ratio, including display scaling and window zoom.
- Keep that ratio local to each workbench window and update it through the existing pixel-ratio monitor when the window's display scale changes.

## Issues addressed

| Severity | Issue | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Low | #337503: an extra leading border appears when the first connected tab is scrolled | Preserve the source cap's square leading-edge state in the overflow cap, and clear the state when clipping is reset. |
| Low | The divider below the tab strip looks heavier at fractional zoom | Use the same snapped stroke width for all four painted card edges. |
| Medium | Review finding: window zoom alone omits monitor DPI | Use each window's effective pixel-ratio monitor and compare the result against native borders, including fractional display scales. |

## Validation

Validation ran with Node 24.22.1 in a clean detached worktree containing only these eight intended changes. Unrelated local edits were excluded from the validation and PR.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run build-fast -- --client-only` | Passed. |
| `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run typecheck-client` | Passed. |
| `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 bash scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/window.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts --reporter dot` | Passed: 186 tests. |
| `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --browser webkit --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/window.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts --grep 'window zoom factors\|device pixel ratios\|compact painted dividers\|preserves the first Connected tab edge\|keeps the connected outline inside the visible scroll area' --reporter dot` | Passed: 5 tests in Chromium and 5 in WebKit. |
| `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.ts src/vs/workbench/browser/window.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts src/vs/workbench/test/browser/window.test.ts` | Passed. |
| `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/browser/media/floatingPanels.css src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/browser/media/connectedEditorTabs.css` | Passed. |
| `npm run -s precommit` (Git hook) | Passed. |
| `git diff --check` | Passed. |

The new regressions were confirmed to fail before the corresponding fixes. Coverage includes first/non-first tab transitions, theme and density changes, fractional zoom, clipping-state cleanup, per-window pixel-ratio isolation, display-change notifications, and listener disposal.

An additional Chromium renderer probe loaded the candidate's actual stylesheet and compared painted strokes with a real CSS border across 36 combinations of display scales (1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, 2×) and zoom factors. All comparisons matched. In particular:

- 125% display scaling at default zoom: painted and native borders both resolve to `0.8px`.
- 2× display scaling at 150% zoom: painted and native borders both resolve to `1px`.

### How to test

1. Enable Modern UI, select Compact density, and open enough files for horizontal tab overflow.
2. Select the first tab and scroll it partly out of view. The sidebar/editor seam should not gain a rounded second border.
3. Check that the divider remains the same thickness through the tab strip, breadcrumbs, and editor body.
4. Repeat with fractional window zoom and display scaling. Switching between first and later tabs should retain the later tabs' normal outlines.

## Visual evidence

A single labeled before/after comparison image is prepared for manual upload. **It is not attached yet.**

The before image was captured from an unmodified detached worktree at the current-main base `6aeca3c02f4cc1f2315efa2644bd2a972ea030c9`. The same worktree was then given only the curated eight-file patch to capture the after image. Both use identical sample files, Dark 2026, Compact density, 172.8% window zoom, a 2× display (effective pixel ratio 3.456), and a 40px tab scroll offset.

The baseline's overflow cap adds a `0.868056px` leading stroke and a `7px` radius; the candidate keeps both at `0px`. The baseline's painted separator remains `1px`, while the candidate matches the native `0.868056px` border. The comparison is cropped to the same sidebar/editor boundary in both captures.

The temporary worktree and capture processes were removed after validation.

## Review status

- Unresolved actionable findings: None.
- Residual risks: A physical Windows desktop and live multi-monitor moves were not exercised; native display-scale rendering and per-window change propagation are covered by the checks above. Screenshot upload and remote CI verification remain outstanding.

title: MCP password inputs are lost on other machines with Settings Sync: encrypted `mcpInputs` is synced but its key is machine-local
body:
## Summary

With Settings Sync enabled on several machines, MCP `promptString` inputs with `"password": true` in the user `mcp.json` keep getting lost. Entering the secrets on machine A makes VS Code prompt for them again on machine B. Entering them on B makes A prompt again, and so on.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.144.0 (2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf), x64
- Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Settings Sync enabled on 3 machines, with "UI State" included
- Each machine uses a different token for the same input IDs (but see below: identical tokens would not help)

## Steps to reproduce

1. On two machines signed into the same Settings Sync account, use a user-level `mcp.json` with a password input:
   ```jsonc
   {
     "inputs": [
       { "type": "promptString", "id": "my-token", "description": "Token", "password": true }
     ],
     "servers": {
       "example": {
         "type": "stdio",
         "command": "some-mcp-server",
         "env": { "TOKEN": "${input:my-token}" }
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. On machine A, start the server and enter the token.
3. Let Settings Sync run, then start the server on machine B. B prompts for the token. Enter it.
4. Let Settings Sync run, then restart the server on machine A.

**Expected:** Each machine keeps its own saved secret.
**Actual:** Machine A prompts for the token again. The machines keep invalidating each other.

## Cause (from reading the source)

In `src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/common/mcpRegistryInputStorage.ts`:
- Secret input values are AES-GCM encrypted into `mcpInputs.secrets` (`{ iv, value }`).
- The encryption key (`mcpEncryptionKey`) is generated per machine and stored in `ISecretStorageService`, which is not synced.

In `src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/common/mcpRegistry.ts`:
```ts
private readonly _profileStorage = new Lazy(() => ... createInstance(McpRegistryInputStorage, StorageScope.PROFILE, StorageTarget.USER));
```
Because of `StorageTarget.USER`, the `mcpInputs` entry, including the encrypted `secrets` blob, is synced as global state. On the receiving machine, `_unsealSecrets()` fails to decrypt with that machine's key, logs `Error unsealing MCP secrets`, sets `secrets = undefined`, and returns `{}`. The user is prompted again, and the newly sealed blob syncs back and breaks the other machine.

Local sync history confirms this: every snapshot in `%APPDATA%\Code\User\sync\globalState\` contains `mcpInputs` with `secrets.iv`/`secrets.value`. The blob size changes between snapshots taken minutes apart (e.g. 3340 → 448 → 912 → 1300 bytes) as different machines overwrite it.

## Possible fixes

- Store the encrypted secrets under a `StorageTarget.MACHINE` key, separate from the plain-text `values`, so only non-secret inputs sync. Or:
- Leave secrets out of the synced payload, or merge per machine, so one machine's undecryptable blob doesn't overwrite another's.

## Workarounds

- Exclude "UI State" from Settings Sync. This also stops other UI state from syncing.
- Don't use `password` inputs. Use `envFile` or `${env:...}` with machine-local values instead.

Follow-up to #344937, addressing [the runtime-before-discovery review comment](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344937#discussion_r4411872991). Refs #343342.

**Stacked on `aeschli/agents/sdk-customization-inventory` while #344937 is open.** Retarget to `main` after the prerequisite lands. This PR contains only the late MCP identity reconciliation fix, not the preceding SDK inventory and hook fallback changes.

### Changes

- Preserve a runtime-published MCP ID when a matching SDK-discovered plugin child arrives later; reconcile the child's source, range, discovery metadata, and inherited enablement into the live entry.
- Derive the known plugin owner for enablement resolution and retain discovered metadata through subsequent runtime updates.
- Apply confirmed runtime defaults to both representations before resolving host-scoped decisions, so discovery refresh cannot restore a stale inherited default.
- Match only unambiguous SDK plugin declarations. Keep unmarked/ambiguous same-name children separate, and do not claim servers whose runtime provenance is user, workspace, or built-in.
- Add controller and Copilot publication regressions for runtime-first ordering, later state/default updates, host override precedence, ownership removal, and source isolation.

No SDK update, protocol schema change, enablement migration, hook behavior change, or UI redesign.

### Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `env -u COPILOT_PROXY_KERBEROS_SPN ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/shared/mcpCustomizationController.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --reporter dot` — 2,456 passed, 1 pre-existing pending.
- `env -u COPILOT_PROXY_KERBEROS_SPN ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/shared/mcpCustomizationController.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --grep 'McpCustomizationController|runtime-first native MCP' --reporter dot` — 41 passed after the final ownership lookup refinement.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/mcpCustomizationController.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/shared/mcpCustomizationController.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts` — passed; the final changed controller also passed a focused rerun.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Direct review covered identity stability, live-state preservation, SDK-default/host-decision precedence, plugin ownership, and source ambiguity. GUI, real-provider integration, and cross-platform packaged validation were not rerun for this follow-up; CI remains required before merge.

title: agentHost: recover interrupted artifact merge automation
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Fixes artifact Autopilot getting stuck with automatic merging enabled after a transient merge preflight failure, as observed while investigating #344951.

- Persist whether a native action is still preparing or may have dispatched its mutation. Reconciliation can safely rule out preflight effects, including after a restart.
- Automatically reconcile interrupted Merge and Mark Ready attempts with a 30-second backoff. Retry confirmed non-dispatched failures only after a fresh eligibility read, without consuming the mutation budget or changing consent.
- Retry transient GitHub observation/reconciliation errors instead of permanently pausing automation.
- Preserve conservative handling of uncertain queue submissions and legacy checkpoints without dispatch evidence. Confirmed successful actions are not resubmitted.

## Validation

Run with Node 24.22.1 using `fnm exec --using=24.22.1`:

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/githubPullRequestArtifactIntegration.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 91 tests.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/artifactIntegrations/githubPullRequestArtifactIntegration.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/githubPullRequestArtifactIntegration.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

The 12 new regression cases cover repeated stale preflights, undispatched preparation failures, restart recovery, disabled consent, fresh CI gating, Mark Ready recovery, direct-merge versus queue ambiguity, transient reconciliation failures, lost success responses, and conservative legacy recovery. No live GitHub mutation was fault-injected locally.

title: copilot: remove never-run simulation tests and orphaned fixtures
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Follow-up to #344484 and #344610, which retired the legacy panel and inline chat simulations but left their fixtures, scenarios and helpers behind.

This removes Copilot simulation test (stest) code that can never run, plus test data and helpers that nothing references anymore. Every remaining suite still covers shipping code, and all 130 remaining scenarios replay from the cache with unchanged scores. No product code, cache recordings or CI gates change.

**506 files deleted, 15 edited (4 insertions, 49,103 deletions).** Almost all of it is test data, so reviewing commit by commit is easiest:

### 1. Remove simulation tests that never run
- The `notebook (mbpp)` suite (61 scenarios). `const shouldEvaluate = 1 >> 1` is always 0, so the suite was permanently optional: CI never ran it, and its code-execution check was unreachable. It had no cache recordings, and 43 of its 61 baseline scores were 0. Its two fixtures, its 61 baseline entries and the Python execution check that only it used go with it.
- `slashDoc.py.stest.ts`. It defined no tests and wasn't registered in `simulationTests.ts`; its helper was only exercised by its own unit test.
- The `stest.skip` "command center" case in `settingsEditorSearchResultsSelector.stest.ts`, skipped since at least the June 2025 open-source import.

### 2. Remove simulation fixtures and helpers left orphaned
- 298 unreferenced files under `test/simulation/fixtures/`, and the 199 files in 17 of the 18 folders under `test/scenarios/` (only `test-cli` is still used). Most were left behind by #344484; a few were unreferenced even before it.
- Modules nothing imports (`toolSimTest.ts`, `validate.ts`, `evaluators/pythonFix.ts`, `fileUtils.ts`), `NoopTestToolsService`, the unused tool-call scenario loaders, and the `setupCase`/`json` scenario fields that only `toolSimTest.ts` used.
- Matching `.eslint-allowed-javascript-files` entries, and a stale `.github/CODENOTIFY` entry for the already deleted `inlineEditCode.stest.ts`.

### 3. Tidy dead code in remaining simulation tests
- Commented-out tests in `notebooks.stest.ts` and `devContainerConfigGenerator.stest.ts`.
- The unreachable `server` provider branch in `inlineEdit.stest.ts`, and the `--runServerPoweredNesProvider` simulator flag that only fed it (no server-powered NES provider exists anymore).
- The `typescript` case in `debugTools.stest.ts`. It passed `['javascript']`, so it sent the same request as the `javascript` case and replayed the same cached response. Its baseline and outcome entries go with it.

## How orphans were identified
- **Fixtures:** a fixture counts as used if a non-fixture source file names its path, or names one of its multi-segment parent folders as a string literal. An independent review arrived at the same set. Kept on purpose: the NES recordings under `fixtures/inlineEdits/` (their loader picks up companion files by convention), the two files `summarizedDocumentRendering.spec.tsx` reads, and `notebook/LICENSE`. The cache-only simulation run is the runtime check: a remaining test that loaded a deleted fixture would fail it.
- **Modules:** import reachability from the real entry points (simulator, simulation workbench and extension, vitest/mocha specs, scripts), plus a search for path-based loads.
- **Authorship:** almost all removed lines date from the June 2025 open-source import. Later edits to them were mechanical, such as the `no-unexternalized-strings` rollout and the `@workspace` removal.

## Deliberately kept
- `test/e2e/cli.stest.ts`: skipped in CI, but its author has kept it up to date for manual runs.
- The switched-off printout in `debugTools.stest.ts`: it generates `KNOWN_DEBUGGABLE_*` in `debuggableCommandIdentifier.ts`.
- Test-framework APIs that now have few or no callers (`ssuite.optional`, `stest.skip`, `fromFixtureDir`).

## Validation
Run on top of `0f33e8274d7` (`main` at the time of writing):
- `npm run typecheck` in `extensions/copilot` (all four projects): passed.
- `npm run eslint -- <the 11 modified .ts files>`: passed. `git diff --check`: clean.
- `node dist/simulationMain.js --ci --require-cache` (what `npm run simulate-ci` runs): passed, "Score unchanged in 130 scenarios". The baseline goes from 192 to 130 entries: the 61 mbpp scenarios and the duplicate `typescript` case, nothing else.
- `npx vitest run` on the 20 spec files that import the touched helpers or read kept fixtures (tool calling, NES pipeline, `simulationOptions`, `summarizedDocumentRendering`): 218 passed, 1 skipped.
- Hygiene `checkNoNewJavaScriptFiles`: passed.
- Each commit was also checked on its own: type check, simulator build and cache-only CI run pass, with no tracked files modified.

title: Leave hidden UI and stylesheets out of copied chat responses
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337527

Copying a selection from a chat response and pasting it into a Markdown-aware input (such as the chat input) could insert content the reader never saw. This included the hidden file changes summary (`0 files changed+0-0`), its file list, and thousands of characters of Monaco list CSS from the list's embedded `<style>` element. The plain-text clipboard flavor was clean. Only the HTML flavor, which chat writes itself when a selection touches a link, carried the leak.

## Cause

When a selection contains links, `ChatListWidget` writes its own `text/html` flavor so links that only resolve inside VS Code are not shared. It built that HTML by cloning the selected DOM, which also cloned elements that are not rendered. Examples are a summary hidden with `display: none`, the body of a collapsed `<details>`, and the `<style>` element that Monaco lists embed. The HTML-to-Markdown converter then printed the stylesheet as text. The response footer's toolbar, an empty `<ul role="toolbar">`, also became a stray `-` list item.

## Changes

- `chatClipboard.ts`: new `cloneVisibleSelection`, moved here from `ChatListWidget.cloneSelectedContents`. It clones the selection together with its ancestors as before. It then leaves out toolbars and elements the reader cannot see. These are elements that are not rendered, and bodies that collapsed sections hide with `visibility: hidden` or `opacity: 0`. `display: contents` wrappers are kept, because their children render. Hidden elements are marked only for the duration of the clone, and the marks are removed in a `finally` block.
- `htmlToMarkdown.ts`: `style`, `script`, `template` and `noscript` elements produce no text. This also covers HTML pasted from other sources.
- Tests: a regression test in `chatClipboard.test.ts` uses a link, a hidden file changes summary with an embedded list stylesheet, and a footer toolbar. It asserts that formatting survives and none of that UI does. A converter test in `htmlToMarkdown.test.ts` covers the dropped element types.

## Validation

- `chatClipboard.test.ts` and `htmlToMarkdown.test.ts` pass, along with eslint on the changed files and `typecheck-client`.
- Manually tested in Code OSS (Agents window). An agent turn edited a file, and I expanded and collapsed its file changes summary. I then selected from that response into the next turn, copied, and pasted into the chat input.

Before (`main`): the paste contains the hidden file list and its stylesheet.

![before-unfixed-paste](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c555ec5e-c38e-4ddd-a01d-f4de0111ec7f)

After (this PR): only content that is visible in the selection.

![after-fixed-paste](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab65a098-2710-4809-820e-b95b5fdea0b2)

Visible chat UI inside the selection, such as the summary header or the response timestamp and model, is still copied, because it is also part of the selected text.

title: Let extensions add PATH entries to Copilot agent host terminals
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/344946

Copilot agent host sessions can't run CLI tools that extensions put on `PATH` through `ExtensionContext.environmentVariableCollection`: the integrated terminal applies those collections, but agent host shells are spawned by the agent host process, which never sees them. Extensions fall back to tools that return absolute executable paths, which then show up as long, versioned commands that permission checks rightly distrust.

This PR lets an extension opt individual `PATH` entries into agent terminals. With it, the agent can call `dbgjs ...` (or any other extension-shipped CLI) by name, and changes take effect for new commands without restarting VS Code or the agent host.

```ts
context.environmentVariableCollection.prepend('PATH', binDir + path.delimiter, {
	applyAtProcessCreation: true,
	applyToAgentTerminals: true,
});
```

## How it works

- **API (proposed):** `terminalAgentEnvironment` adds `EnvironmentVariableMutatorOptions.applyToAgentTerminals`. Setting it without the proposal throws.
- **Workbench:** `AgentHostTerminalContribution` collects the opted-in, global `PATH` prepend/append mutators of the **local** extension host (absolute directories only) and pushes them to the **local** agent host as the root config key `agentTerminalPath`, re-pushing whenever environment collections change. Remote windows don't push it.
- **Agent host:**
  - The key is transient: it is published in root state but never written to `agent-host-config.json`.
  - Copilot SDK shell commands (the default, and the only option on Windows) get the directories through the shell init script, prepended to any client script. Each directory is added only if missing, since the script runs before every command in a long-lived shell. This applies even when the client shell-init setting is off.
  - Shells of the agent host's custom terminal tool get the directories in their spawn environment.

Only `PATH` entries are forwarded on purpose. Collections also carry things like git askpass variables and Python activation that don't belong in agent shells.

## Validation

- Unit tests: proposal check and serialization in the ext host, forwarding/filtering in the workbench contribution, transient persistence in the agent host configuration service, and init-script generation. The PowerShell prelude is executed for real (order, idempotence, quoting); the bash variant runs on non-Windows CI.
- End to end in Code OSS on Windows with a probe extension that prepends a `bin` folder with `applyToAgentTerminals: true`, in a Copilot (agent host) session:
  - `agentpathprobe` resolved from the extension folder.
  - After disabling the entry, a new session got "not recognized".
  - After re-enabling it, the same session resolved it again, without any restart.

## Limitations / open questions

- Shells already running keep a removed entry until they exit, since the init script only adds.
- Being a proposed API, marketplace extensions can't use it yet; the first consumer is the dbgjs extension.
- Should the opt-in also cover the Copilot Chat (`run_in_terminal`) terminal, which already gets the full collection today?

title: Let extensions add PATH entries to Copilot agent host terminals

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

body:
Extensions can add directories to `PATH` for the integrated terminal with `ExtensionContext.environmentVariableCollection`. Copilot Chat's terminal tool picks these up, but Copilot agent host sessions do not: their shells are spawned by the agent host process, which never sees extension environment collections.

So a tool an extension ships (for example the `dbgjs` CLI bundled with the dbgjs extension) can't be called by its name in agent host sessions. The only workaround is an extension tool that returns the absolute executable path, which leads to long, versioned commands into the extensions folder. Permission checks such as assisted auto-approve rightly treat those as suspicious and ask for confirmation.

**Proposal:** let an extension mark individual `PATH` entries of its environment variable collection as intended for agent terminals:

```ts
context.environmentVariableCollection.prepend('PATH', binDir + path.delimiter, {
	applyAtProcessCreation: true,
	applyToAgentTerminals: true, // proposed: terminalAgentEnvironment
});
```

The local agent host then adds these directories to `PATH` of the shells its agents run commands in, so the agent can run `dbgjs ...` directly. Changes apply to new commands without restarting VS Code or the agent host.

The opt-in is deliberately narrow: only global `PATH` prepend/append entries that are absolute directories qualify, and only from the local extension host to the local agent host. Other environment mutations (askpass variables, Python activation, ...) are not forwarded.

title: Agent host: chat created while the remote host connection is down cannot be restored (Session identity was not advertised)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

body:
When the connection to a remote agent host is down and VS Code has stopped reconnecting, sending the first message in a new chat for that host still creates a chat session on the client only. The host never creates it. After a reload, that chat's editor can't be restored and shows *"The editor could not be opened due to an unexpected error"*. **Try Again** keeps failing, and the prompt is lost.

Version: 1.145.0-insider (commit c5f99e81a5d0ce82a55615da27c322bbe48ad00e), Windows, remote agent host over WebSocket (`copilotcli` provider).

## What happened (reconstructed from the renderer log)

1. The WebSocket connection to the remote agent host closed. `RemoteAgentHostProtocol` retried in rounds (`Automatic reconnect to <host> gave up after 10 attempts.`, followed by `Connection closed` and another round). After about 20 minutes, the rounds stopped. The window then stayed disconnected from that host for about 12 hours, with no further reconnect attempts in the log.
2. In that state, I opened a new chat for that host and sent a message:
   ```
   [info]  ChatService#materializeUntitledSession: Materialized untitled session <host>-copilotcli:/untitled-<uuid> into real session <host>-copilotcli:/<id>
   [info]  [AgentHost] _invokeAgent called for resource: <host>-copilotcli:/<id>
   [error] Error while handling chat request: Automatic reconnect gave up after 10 attempts.: Error: Automatic reconnect gave up after 10 attempts.
   ```
   The request failed immediately, but the editor kept the materialized resource `/<id>`. The same failure had already happened once with an earlier new chat.
3. Later, the window reconnected to the host and was reloaded. Restoring that chat editor fails, and so does every **Try Again**:
   ```
   [error] ChatService#loadRemoteSession: failed to restore <host>-copilotcli:/<id> Session identity was not advertised by its agent host: <host>-copilotcli:/<id>
   [error] Error: Failed to get model for chat editor. resource: <host>-copilotcli:/<id>
   ```
   The error comes from `_discoverSessionIdentity` in [agentHostSessionHandler.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c5f99e81a5d0ce82a55615da27c322bbe48ad00e/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts). It refreshes identities through `connection.listSessions()`, and the ID isn't listed. I confirmed with an AHP `listSessions` call directly against the host: neither a session nor a chat with that ID exists. The host never received the session.

## Problems

1. **No recovery after reconnect gives up.** Once automatic reconnect stops, the host connection stays dead indefinitely, but the UI still lets you start chats and send messages to that host. The failure only appears after sending.
2. **The untitled session is materialized before the host confirms it.** If creating the session or sending the first message fails, the editor keeps a resource that will never exist on the host. That leaves an editor that can't be restored, and the user's prompt is lost.

## Expected

- Keep reconnecting periodically (or on window focus or network change), or clearly show that the host is disconnected and block sending until it is reachable again.
- If the first request fails before the host creates the session, keep or revert the chat as untitled and keep the prompt, so the user can resend it once the host is back.
- When a restored chat refers to a session the host doesn't know, show a specific message instead of the generic "editor could not be opened" error.

title: agentHost: record a nested session's own conversation so it can move back out
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #344917

## Problem

A session nested under another session couldn't be moved back out. **Move to New Session** and **Undo** were both refused with "This chat has no conversation of its own yet, so it can't be moved into a new session" (`_checkPromotable`, `AgentChatMoveRefusal.Unsupported`), so the session stayed nested for good.

## Cause

Regression from #342904 (C15).

- Older sessions record no backing for their main chat (`chats_v2.provider_data` is NULL). Their agent (Copilot, Claude or Codex) derives the backing from the session when the session is restored in full (`materializeChat` with no provider data), and the host then records it.
- Since #342904, a move loads a session that isn't loaded with its data only, and its agent never sees it. So nothing recorded the backing, and the nest moved the chat without one. `_checkPromotable` then refused every later move to a new session.
- Sessions that were loaded or that already had a backing were fine. Legacy (authority-1) catalogs are always restored in full, so they were fine too.
- In the reporter's database, 118 of 774 normalized sessions (about 15%) have a main chat without a recorded backing.

## Fix

In `agentService.ts`:

1. `_movedSessionChat` loads the source with its data only when its main chat records a backing (`_recordsDefaultChatBacking`, which reads the recorded catalog and never derives anything from a chat URI). Otherwise it restores the source in full, where the agent derives the backing and the host records it, so the nest carries it.
2. Safety net: before any session moves under another, `_checkChatMoveRequest` refuses the move (`NotMovable`) if the main chat still records no backing, and nothing changes. A read failure becomes the same refusal. With today's agents this shouldn't trigger, since all three derive a backing.

Already stuck sessions are not repaired (out of scope).

**Cost.** The full restore only happens when nesting a session that isn't loaded and whose main chat has no recorded backing (about 15% of sessions in the reporter's database). It costs the same as opening that session once: the agent resumes its SDK session to read the history. The session is released again by the normal residency rules. Sessions that are loaded, or that already have a backing, take the C15 data-only path as before; a test assertion and the live log both show this.

**Refusal text.** For a refused session nest, the sessions list shows "Could not move session '{title}'. This chat can't be moved." There's no URI in it. This couldn't be triggered live because every current agent derives a backing, so the unit tests cover it.

## Tests

New tests are in the C15 suite of `agentService.test.ts`:
- **Old session (#344917):** a session that isn't loaded and has no backing nests with its backing recorded, and moves back out. Red before the fix: backing `undefined`, the move back refused `unsupported`.
- **Legacy session:** an authority-1 session that isn't loaded does the same.
- **Agent records no backing:** the nest is refused, loaded or not and via the `move_session` check, and nothing changes.
- **Unreadable catalog:** a session whose chats can't be read is refused as `NotMovable`.
- **C15 unchanged:** the existing test now asserts that a session with a backing still nests with its data only.

Test agents now report a backing like the real agents do. `MockAgent.initialChatProviderData` is unset by default; `MovingAgent` and `ChatAgent` set it, and `MovingAgent.materializeChat` derives one for chats stored in their session's database. This removed four tests' hand-written `UPDATE chats_v2 SET provider_data` workarounds; their assertions are unchanged.

Mutation checks: dropping the full restore, the safety net, or the error conversion each fails its own test.

Runs:
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/**/*.test.js"`: **passed**, 13934 passing, 0 failing.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: **passed**.
- `npm run eslint -- <4 changed files>`: **passed**.

## Live check

Code - OSS Agents window, throwaway profile, Copilot only.

To make old sessions, I cleared the main chat's backing in that profile only and gave the SDK session the session's id, as in pre-backing sessions.

- **Unfixed:** Move to New Session and Undo were refused with the reporter's message, and the nested rows had `provider_data` NULL, matching the reporter's logs.
- **Fixed:**
  - Nesting an old session that isn't loaded, then **Undo**, works; so does nesting one and then **Move to New Session**.
  - The promoted session continues its old conversation, and it stays its own session after a restart.
  - A fresh session with a backing still nests with no SDK resume (data-only).
- **Not covered live:** the refusal, since no current agent leaves the backing unrecorded.

## Review

Independent code review approved. It found that the error conversion was missing; that is fixed and covered by a test.

title: Test: Multiple harnesses in one Agents-window session (Copilot, Claude and Codex chats side by side)
body:
- [ ] macOS
- [ ] linux
- [ ] windows

Complexity: 5

Authors: @sandy081

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23344927%0A%0A&assignees=sandy081)

---

In 1.145, one Agents-window session can hold chats on different harnesses, for example a Claude and a Codex nested session in a Copilot session. Each chat keeps its own harness, model and approvals when you move or fork it, and across restarts. The feature is behind `chat.agentHost.multipleChatProviders.enabled` (off by default); moves between agents also need `chat.agentHost.moveChats.enabled` (on by default in Insiders).

## Setup

1. Update to the latest **Insiders** (it must contain #344685).
2. Create a throwaway Git folder with one commit:
   - macOS / Linux: `mkdir ~/tpi-harness && cd ~/tpi-harness && git init && echo "# TPI harness" > README.md && git add . && git commit -m init`
   - Windows (cmd): `mkdir %USERPROFILE%\tpi-harness && cd /d %USERPROFILE%\tpi-harness && git init && echo # TPI harness> README.md && git add . && git commit -m init`
3. Launch Insiders with a fresh profile folder, opening the Agents window (your normal Insiders can stay open):

   | OS | Command |
   |---|---|
   | macOS | `"/Applications/Visual Studio Code - Insiders.app/Contents/Resources/app/bin/code-insiders" --user-data-dir ~/tpi-harness-data --agents` |
   | Windows (cmd) | `"%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Microsoft VS Code Insiders\bin\code-insiders.cmd" --user-data-dir %USERPROFILE%\tpi-harness-data --agents` |
   | Linux | `code-insiders --user-data-dir ~/tpi-harness-data --agents` |

4. Sign in to GitHub (Claude and Codex use it too). If `chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled` or `chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled` is greyed out in **Settings**, your organization manages it: skip that harness.
5. In **Settings**, leave `chat.agentHost.multipleChatProviders.enabled` **off** (scenario 1 turns it on) and check that `chat.agentHost.moveChats.enabled` is on.
6. In **New Session**, with the Git folder, create these sessions by **Session Type**, send "say hi" in each, and **Rename...** them:
   - **CP** (Copilot), **CL** (Claude), **CX** and **CX2** (Codex).

> Only move sessions you created in this test.

## How to test

Do the scenarios in order. A chat on another harness than its session's names that harness in its **tab hover** (for example "say hi (Claude)") and its **Sessions-list hover**, and its **model picker** lists only its harness's models.

Steps marked 🧪 haven't been tried with real agents yet. Tell us whatever happens.

## Scenario 1: Turn the feature on without a reload

1. In **CP**, click **+** on its row (**New Nested Session**, <kbd>Cmd+T</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl+T</kbd>), type "draft text" without sending, and click **Show Session Options**.
   - **Expected:** no harness picker.
2. Keep the composer open and turn on `chat.agentHost.multipleChatProviders.enabled` in **Settings**.
   - **Expected:** a harness picker showing **Copilot** appears within a second; no reload; "draft text" is kept.

## Scenario 2: Pick the harness of a nested session

1. Open the harness picker.
   - **Expected:** it lists **Copilot**, **Claude** and **Codex** (screen reader: "Pick Harness for New Chat, Copilot").
2. Pick **Claude** and send "say hi and tell me which model you are".
   - **Expected:** Claude answers in a new nested session of CP; its hovers name **Claude**; Claude models only.
3. Add nested sessions to **CP** with **Codex**, and with **Copilot**.
   - **Expected:** the Codex one names **Codex** and lists Codex models; the Copilot one names no harness.
4. In **CL**, add a nested session with **Copilot**.
   - **Expected:** its hovers name **Copilot**; Copilot models.
5. In a new nested composer, switch the harness quickly several times (also by keyboard: <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the picker, <kbd>Enter</kbd>, arrows, <kbd>Enter</kbd>), then type and send right away.
   - **Expected:** the last pick answers; typed text is kept; no empty chat tabs are left.

## Scenario 3: Each chat has its own model and approvals

Use **CP** and its nested sessions.

title: Improve Agent Skills discoverability, grouping, and invocation semantics
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
## Problem

The current Agent Skill UI makes it difficult to understand which skills are available, where they come from, and when they will be used.

Skills from different sources appear to be mixed together, including:

- VS Code built-in Copilot skills
- Skills provided by installed extensions
- Workspace or user-defined skills
- Multiple installed versions of the same extension

As a result, users may see duplicated skills, overlapping descriptions, and skills with similar names but different scopes or invocation rules. It is also unclear whether selecting a skill enables it, invokes it immediately, or only changes the agent's available context.

## Current behavior

- Skill groups are difficult to distinguish.
- The source extension or scope of a skill is not always obvious.
- Similar or duplicated skills can appear together without explanation.
- Skill descriptions use inconsistent levels of detail and terminology.
- The relationship between automatic invocation, user invocation, and manual selection is unclear.
- Conflicts or overlaps between skills are not surfaced to the user.

## Expected behavior

The UI should make the following information explicit for every skill:

- Skill name and short purpose
- Source: built-in, extension, workspace, or user
- Scope: current workspace, global, or extension-specific
- Invocation mode: automatic, user-invocable, or disabled for automatic invocation
- Whether the skill is currently enabled or merely available
- Extension version when relevant

Skills should also be grouped by source and purpose, with duplicated or overridden skills clearly identified.

## Proposed improvements

1. Group skills by source first, such as Built-in, Extension-provided, Workspace, and User.
2. Add filters for source, scope, invocation mode, and enabled state.
3. Show a concise, normalized description format for every skill.
4. Display badges such as `Built-in`, `Extension`, `Workspace`, `Automatic`, and `Manual`.
5. Detect duplicate names and show which version or source takes precedence.
6. Explain what happens when a user selects or enables a skill.
7. Provide a details view containing the skill's invocation rules and source file.
8. Add a warning when multiple skills may match the same request.

## Why this matters

Skills are becoming an important extension point for Agent mode. Without clear grouping and invocation semantics, users cannot reliably predict which workflow will run, troubleshoot unexpected behavior, or safely configure their own skills.

## Environment

- OS: Windows

## Additional context

This issue is about discoverability, grouping, and selection semantics rather than the content of any individual skill.

title: Agent Debug Logs: no data for active agent-host (Copilot CLI) sessions until VS Code restart — live events never stream
body:
### Description

The Agent Debug Logs panel shows no data for **active** agent-host (Copilot CLI) chat sessions — the Summary reports 0 model turns / 0 tool calls / 0 total tokens and the Logs view is empty — for every session created during the current VS Code run. The data only becomes visible **after fully restarting VS Code**, when the panel loads the persisted session files. Live inspection is effectively impossible.

### Environment

- VS Code: 1.144.0 (commit `2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf`), stable
- OS: Linux x64 (Arch-based, kernel 7.2.8-9-omarchy, Wayland)
- Copilot Chat: built-in extension `copilot-chat` 0.72.0
- Settings enabled:
  - `chat.agentHost.agentDebugLog.enabled: true`
  - `github.copilot.chat.agentDebugLog.fileLogging.enabled: true`
- Chat sessions run through the Agent Host (separate `copilot-runtime` process, provider `copilotcli`)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable both debug log settings and fully restart VS Code.
2. Open a workspace, start a new chat (agent) session and send a few prompts that trigger tool calls.
3. While VS Code is still running, open the Agent Debug Logs panel (Chat view `...` menu → *Show Agent Debug Logs*, or *Developer: Open Agent Debug Logs*) and select the active session.
4. Observe: Summary shows all zeros (model turns, tool calls, total input tokens), Logs view shows no events. Any additional session created during this run behaves the same.
5. Fully quit and restart VS Code, open the panel again.
6. The sessions from steps 2–4 now show complete data (events, turns, tool calls, token totals). New sessions created after the restart again show nothing until the *next* restart.

### Diagnostics (evidence that the data itself is being captured)

While the active session shows nothing in the panel:

- The runtime writes the full event stream **live** to `~/.copilot/session-state/<uuid>/events.jsonl` (mtime follows the conversation in real time). Verified event types include `session.start`, `user.message`, `assistant.turn_start/end`, `tool.execution_start/complete`, `model.model_call_started/success`, `model.turn_started/ended` and `session.usage_record` carrying `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`/`cacheReadTokens`/`reasoningTokens`.
- The active session's file only lacks a `session.shutdown` event — i.e. it is the live one.
- `/proc/<pid>/fd` shows **no process holding an open fd** on the active session's `events.jsonl`, and `/proc/<pid>/fdinfo` shows **no inotify watch** on the session file or its directory — the live tail appears to never be established.
- File watching in the same VS Code instance works fine: it inotify-watches the workspace root and the `~/.copilot/session-state` root, so this is not a watcher/inotify problem (limits 1024 instances / 524288 watches, ~68 in use; no ENOSPC in kernel log).
- `copilot-runtime` is alive and connected to the window via an anonymous socketpair (ESTAB).
- After a restart the panel renders those sessions correctly, proving the historical/discovery path can read the files — only the **live path for sessions of the current run** is broken.

Additional context: this machine switched from the old debug-logs location (`workspaceStorage/<hash>/GitHub.copilot-chat/debug-logs/<sessionId>/main.jsonl`, last written Oct 4) to the agent-host location (`~/.copilot/session-state/...`) on Oct 9, when chat sessions moved onto the Agent Host architecture (#325417). The symptom appeared together with that switch.

### Workaround

Reading the file directly shows everything live:

```bash
tail -f "$(ls -t ~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl | head -1)"
```

### Related

- #303356 — CLI sessions only appeared after the second message (same discovery path)
- #309261 / #309073 — historical sessions + live events when continuing them
- #325417 — agent-host support in the panel (reads `events.jsonl`, usage sidecar)
- #302209 — same "only works after restart" pattern on the settings side (macOS)

body:
In today's Insiders, a session that was nested under another session can't be moved back out.

**Steps**
1. Have an older session that isn't open in the Agents window (in my case a 4-month-old worktree session).
2. Drag it onto another session to nest it. The nest succeeds.
3. On the nested chat, run **Move to New Session** (or click **Undo** in the move notice).

**Expected:** the chat becomes its own session again.

**Actual:** the move fails every time. The agent host refuses it with:

> Chat ahp-chat://default/… has no recorded conversation of its own to take into a new session.

(`AgentChatMoveRefusal.Unsupported`, from `_checkPromotable` in `agentService.ts`.)

The session's data is intact, but it stays stuck under the other session. Undo fails the same way, because Undo of a nest also moves the chat to a new session.

**Cause (from the logs and the agent-host database):** after the nest, the moved session's main chat has no provider data in `chats_v2`, i.e. no link to its own conversation. The destination session's own main chat does have it. The nest didn't record that link for the moved chat. Nests of sessions that were already loaded keep working; the one that failed here was an older session that wasn't loaded at the time of the nest.

title: Return an unsigned value from readUInt32LE
body:
## Problem

`readUInt32LE` returns a **signed** number whenever bit 31 is set, while its big-endian sibling `readUInt32BE` returns an unsigned one:

```ts
const buff = VSBuffer.alloc(4);
buff.writeUInt32LE(0xDEADBEEF, 0);
buff.readUInt32LE(0);   // -559038737, expected 3735928559
```

The cause is in the combination itself: each byte term is coerced with `>>> 0`, but the final `|` of the four terms produces an int32, so the high bit comes back as a sign bit. `readUInt32BE` avoids this by summing products (`source[offset] * 2 ** 24 + ...`) instead of bitwise OR.

There is a workaround in the tree that shows the trap is real: `src/vs/base/test/common/zip.test.ts` reads the CRC as `archive.readUInt32LE(14) >>> 0`.

## Fix

Coerce the combined value once:

```ts
export function readUInt32LE(source: Uint8Array, offset: number): number {
	return (
		((source[offset + 0] << 0) >>> 0) |
		((source[offset + 1] << 8) >>> 0) |
		((source[offset + 2] << 16) >>> 0) |
		((source[offset + 3] << 24) >>> 0)
	) >>> 0;
}
```

## Tests

One assertion added to the existing `Buffer` suite in `src/vs/base/test/common/buffer.test.ts`, next to the existing round-trip case.

Without the fix:


title: Fix isValidBasename rejecting valid Windows names with leading or Unicode whitespace

title: Explorer rejects valid Windows file names with a leading space or Unicode whitespace, and accepts control characters
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: main @ d7658021
- OS Version: Windows 11

On Windows, creating or renaming a file in the Explorer to ` notes.md` (leading space), `メモ　.txt` (U+3000 ideographic space) or `a` + U+00A0 shows "The name … is not valid as a file or folder name", although Windows accepts all of these (only a trailing space or dot is stripped). The other way round, a name containing a control character (U+0001–U+001F) passes validation and then fails when the file is written.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In the Explorer on Windows, create a new file named ` notes.md` (with a leading space).
2. The input shows the "not valid as a file or folder name" error instead of the leading/trailing-whitespace warning other platforms show.

In code: `isValidBasename(' a.txt', true)` and `isValidBasename('a　', true)` return `false`, and `isValidBasename('a\^Ab', true)` returns `true`. Creating the same names through Win32 `CreateFileW` (e.g. Python `open(name, 'x')`) succeeds for the first two and fails for the third.

**Root cause.** In `src/vs/base/common/extpath.ts`, `name.length !== name.trim().length` is meant to catch a trailing space, but `trim()` also strips leading and Unicode whitespace. `WINDOWS_INVALID_FILE_CHARS` leaves out characters 1–31, which the [Windows naming rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file) forbid.

**Suggested fix.** Check only for a trailing `' '`, and add `\^@-\^_` to the invalid set; the Explorer's existing whitespace warning then applies on Windows as on other platforms. I have a patch with a test and will open a PR linked to this issue.

title: mcp: cancel the server request named by notifications/cancelled
body:
Fixes #344911

A server's `notifications/cancelled` names a request the server sent, but the handler cancelled the editor's own pending request with that ID: sampling and elicitation were never cancelled, a matching editor request was aborted, and ID 0 was ignored. `JsonRpcProtocol` now tracks incoming requests and exposes `cancelIncomingRequest`, and the handler uses it.

The response is still sent after cancellation (the spec says SHOULD NOT); I left that as is to keep this change to the token.

Testing:
- Replaced the test that asserted the old behaviour; the new one fails on main (tokens `[false, false]`) and passes with the fix.
- Added a `jsonRpcProtocol.test.ts` case for `cancelIncomingRequest`.
- MCP common/node unit tests and `vs/base/test/common` pass; eslint is clean. Not tried in a running build.

title: MCP: server's notifications/cancelled cancels the editor's own request instead of the server's sampling/elicitation request
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: main @ d7658021df (found in source and the MCP unit tests; not checked in a running build)
- OS Version: Windows 11

When an MCP server cancels a request it sent to VS Code (for example `elicitation/create` timing out, which the TypeScript SDK does after 60s by default), VS Code doesn't cancel that request: the elicitation prompt stays open and sampling keeps running. Instead, if the cancelled ID matches one of VS Code's own in-flight requests (the two sides number their requests independently), that unrelated request, such as a `tools/call`, is rejected as Canceled.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Run an MCP server on the TypeScript SDK (1.32.2) whose tool calls `server.server.elicitInput(..., { timeout: 1000 })`.
2. Call the tool from VS Code and let the elicitation time out.
3. The server sends `{"method":"elicitation/create",...,"id":0}` and then `{"method":"notifications/cancelled","params":{"requestId":0,"reason":"McpError: MCP error -32001: Request timed out"}}`. The prompt stays open.

**Root cause.** `mcpServerRequestHandler.ts` `handleCancelledNotification` calls `this._rpc.cancelPendingRequest(requestId)`, which only looks at the editor's outgoing requests. Per the spec, and the bundled schema (`CancelledNotificationParams.requestId`: "MUST correspond to the ID of a request previously issued in the same direction"), the ID names a server→client request. `JsonRpcProtocol._handleRequest` doesn't keep the handler's cancellation token, so nothing can cancel it. Also, `if (request.params.requestId)` skips ID 0, which is the SDK's first request ID.

**Suggested fix.** Track incoming requests' cancellation tokens by ID in `JsonRpcProtocol`, add `cancelIncomingRequest(id)`, and call it from the handler with a `!== undefined` check; the elicitation and sampling services already honour the token. I have a patch with tests and will open a PR linked to this issue.

Clicking any VS Code UI component outside the Integrated Browser should transfer focus to that component.

The Integrated Browser should release focus when the user clicks elsewhere in the VS Code workbench.

The Integrated Browser retains focus when attempting to switch to other VS Code UI components using the mouse.

title: Agents window: drag and drop onto a workspace revealed by "+N more workspaces" does nothing

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (core Agents window sessions list)

- VS Code Version: 1.145.0 (`main` @ d7658021df8; root cause verified in code)
- OS Version: macOS (not OS-specific)

In the Agents window sessions list, workspaces can be reordered with drag and drop. When the capped workspaces are expanded with "+N more workspaces", there is an implicit line between the always-visible workspaces and the revealed ones. Any drop onto a revealed workspace fails: a drop indicator is shown, but the dragged item doesn't move there. It doesn't matter what is dragged: a workspace from above the line, another revealed workspace or a custom group.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In the Agents window, group sessions by Workspace, Repository or Environment, with Show > Recent (the default).
2. Have at least one workspace with a session updated in the last 4 days and at least two workspaces whose sessions are all older than that, so a "+N more workspaces" row appears.
3. Click "+N more workspaces" to reveal the capped workspaces.
4. Drag any workspace, from above the line or from the revealed ones, and drop it before or after one of the revealed workspaces.
5. 🐛 The drop indicator is shown, but nothing moves.

For comparison, dropping onto a workspace above the line works, including when a revealed workspace is dragged there: it moves up and stays visible after collapsing.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

- `update()` puts only custom groups and primary (uncapped) workspaces in the user-managed `_topLevelOrder`. Revealed "+N more" workspaces are appended after that block in their default order and aren't part of it ([sessionsList.ts#L5725-L5776](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d7658021df8289f549bf2af8c8dec131f2580d69/src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts#L5725-L5776)).
- `getHeaderDrop` returns a `topLevel` drop for any top-level grouping section, including revealed ones, so the drop feedback looks valid ([sessionsList.ts#L7089-L7101](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d7658021df8289f549bf2af8c8dec131f2580d69/src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts#L7089-L7101)).
- `applyHeaderDrop` calls `ISessionSectionOrderService.reorder(this._topLevelOrder, ...)` ([sessionsList.ts#L7154-L7164](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d7658021df8289f549bf2af8c8dec131f2580d69/src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts#L7154-L7164)). `spliceSectionOrder` requires only the drop target, not the dragged item, to be in that order. When the target isn't there, it returns `undefined` and `reorder` silently returns ([sessionSectionOrderService.ts#L129-L133](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d7658021df8289f549bf2af8c8dec131f2580d69/src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/browser/sessionSectionOrderService.ts#L129-L133), [#L262-L275](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d7658021df8289f549bf2af8c8dec131f2580d69/src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/browser/sessionSectionOrderService.ts#L262-L275)).
- Before that, `applyHeaderDrop` moves the dragged header to the top level, so a header dragged out of a custom group leaves its group but doesn't land where it was dropped.

Drops onto headers above the line work because the target is in `_topLevelOrder`. A revealed workspace dragged there is also promoted so it escapes capping, by design (#322916). The `organizeSessionsList` tool already rejects revealed workspaces as targets explicitly ([sessionsList.ts#L7413-L7415](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d7658021df8289f549bf2af8c8dec131f2580d69/src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts#L7413-L7415)).

</details>

### Expected behavior

Dropping onto a revealed workspace should move the dragged item there, the same as dropping onto a workspace above the line. A workspace moved below the line should land where it's dropped and be hidden behind "+N more workspaces" when collapsed, until it's dragged back up.

Only promotion exists today (there's no demotion state), so this leaves some design questions:

- Capping is criteria-based, not a fixed count. A workspace stays above the line if it has a comparison group, a session updated in the last 4 days, the open window's folder or the onboarding session, if it has been promoted, or if it's the most-recent fallback ([sessionsList.ts#L5455-L5498](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d7658021df8289f549bf2af8c8dec131f2580d69/src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts#L5455-L5498)). If the visible block had a fixed size, the first workspace below the line might need to move up when one is moved down.
- Should a moved-down workspace stay below the line when it gets new activity, or return above it?
- Reordering revealed workspaces among themselves needs a persisted order for the revealed area. Today any successful drag also promotes the dragged workspace, which would move it above the line instead of where it was dropped.
- What should happen when a custom group, which is never capped, is dropped below the line?

At minimum, the list shouldn't show a drop indicator for a drop that has no effect.

*🤖 Written by GitHub Copilot on behalf of @jruales.*

title: chat: show attachments as inline pills in the prompt
body: Adds an experimental `chat.inlineAttachments.enabled` setting, off by default so the existing attachment flow is unchanged, that renders chat attachments as pills inline with the prompt at the position where they were added instead of above the input. Each pill keeps the existing attachment pill UX, including its remove button, and occupies a single anchor character in the input, so the cursor, selection, deletion, copy and paste, and undo and redo treat it as one character: the pill right before the cursor is highlighted, Backspace deletes it along with its attachment, and Enter opens it. This covers files and folders (dropped or picked), `#` and `@` references, tools, symbols, instructions, source control commits, problems, pull request and issue links, pasted text, and terminal commands, while images keep the existing treatment above the input, and a tool that the request would not use, such as one that is turned off, is shown dashed. A projection expands each pill back to the text it stands for, which is what gets parsed, sent, persisted, and restored from history, and sent requests show the same pills inline in the request bubble with images above it. It also fixes the editor's DOM line break computation for lines that contain inline blocks so that pills wrap correctly, adds accessibility help and screen reader announcements for pills, and adds unit tests for the projection, the parser, line breaking, undo and redo, and moving text with pills.

title: Replace @vscode and #vscodeAPI with a built-in vscode skill
body:
Replace the `@vscode` chat participant (`github.copilot.vscode`, including its `/search` command) and the `#vscodeAPI` tool (`copilot_getVSCodeAPI`) in the Local (Copilot Chat extension) harness with a built-in `vscode` skill in core. The skill tells the agent to answer questions about using, configuring and extending VS Code from VS Code's own sources: the docs index, release notes, the extension API typings, and the live settings and command registries. It is backed by three VS Code tools that let the agent find settings and commands, change a setting, or run a command, always after the user confirms.

The skill is offered to Copilot agent host sessions in both the editor window and the Agents window. Preserve the settings and command embeddings, which the Command Palette, the Settings editor AI search and the new `findVSCodeSettingsAndCommands` tool all use, and the ordinary docs and tool search flows.

Related precedent: #344452, #343118.

Plan: first add the `vscode` skill and its tools, then deprecate and remove `@vscode` and `#vscodeAPI` once the skill has shipped. Document the deprecation and removal in the release notes for the release that removes them.

### 1. Add the `vscode` skill

## Summary

Remove `chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable` and make its enabled behavior unconditional. Remove the setting registration, setting ID, host readers, disabled branches, flag-only arguments, and obsolete tests across the Agent Host providers, editor chat, Agents window, and Copilot extension.

- Desktop users can continue into the Agents window without GitHub sign-in. Copilot remains selectable for model setup; Claude native credentials and Codex provider authentication remain available without GitHub.

- Keep the Copilot extension's utility-model hint scoped to local chat.

**ExP is intentionally untouched.** Its retirement is separate and must wait until this change ships to stable.

title: testing: respect keybindings before type-to-filter
body:
Fixes #344598.

The Test Explorer handles printable keydown events before normal command dispatch. Even when soft dispatch has found a user shortcut, its listener replaces the filter text and focuses the filter input, invalidating the shortcut's tree-focus context before the command can execute.

Inject `IKeybindingService` into the existing view model and start type-to-filter only when `softDispatch` returns `NoMatchingKb`. Matching commands and chord prefixes keep their current focus and filter text; unbound printable keys still start filtering.

Five DOM-level cases render `TestingExplorerView` with controlled keybinding-resolution results. They cover `j/k/o`, a chord prefix, unchanged existing filter text and tree focus, and the unbound printable-key fallback. The fixture reuses workbench test services and owns its created UI resources.

Validation on Linux, Node 24.22.1, using the repository Electron runner:
- Four shortcut/chord regressions fail against the original production code; the unbound-key control passes.
- Fixed view plus related tree/list projection and filter-state suites: **31 passing**.
- Client transpilation (`npm run build-fast -- --client-only`), changed-file ESLint, hygiene, and `git diff --check` passed.

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --no-sandbox --ozone-platform=headless --disable-gpu \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/testing/test/browser/testingExplorerView.test.ts \
```

title: agentHost: retry failed Mission Control session registration
body:
Fixes #344519.

After a transient Git repository-root or remotes lookup failure, `MissionControlSessionPublisher` retains a rejected `ready` promise. Every subsequent registration, including the SDK source's scheduled retry, receives that original rejection even after Git recovers.

Retry failed registrations on the next `registerSession` call while continuing to share in-flight and successful registrations. Action dispatch still skips a failed publication instead of starting Git probes for every incoming action. Count discarded buffered and subsequent AHP actions as source lag so SDK metadata can recover without silently publishing incomplete AHP history.

Three regression cases cover root/remotes lookup recovery, repeated failure, coalesced retries, successful cache reuse, and SDK publication alongside a retained AHP integrity failure.

Validation on Linux with Node 24.22.1 and the repository Electron runner:
- Original publisher plus new tests: **26 passing, 3 failing**.
- Fixed publisher, mirror, and SDK event-source suites: **79 passing**.
- Client transpilation (`npm run build-fast -- --client-only`), changed-file ESLint, hygiene, and `git diff --check` passed.

title: agentHost: preserve selection answer kinds for freeform replies
body:
Fixes #344676.

A freeform-only reply to a selection question currently falls through to a `Text` answer. A conforming Agent Host expects the answer kind to match the question, so the submission can be rejected while the session remains waiting.

This change uses the question metadata in that fallback:
- Single-select replies become `Selected` with an empty selection and `freeformValues`.
- Multi-select replies become `SelectedMany` with an empty selection list and `freeformValues`.
- Text questions and callers without question metadata keep the existing text fallback.

title: Let dictation reach chat inputs contributed by extensions (webviews), including over Remote Tunnels
body:
## The Gap

Built-in dictation and the VS Code Speech extension write only into inputs the workbench owns. Those are the Chat view, editors and similar rich inputs, and the terminal. A chat panel an extension contributes as a webview gets nothing. Two widely used examples are the Claude Code extension (anthropic.claude-code) and the Codex extension (openai.chatgpt). With one of those panels focused, the microphone button, `Ctrl+I` and `Ctrl+Alt+V` do nothing for it.

This matters most over a Remote Tunnel or SSH. Dictation runs on the client, which is the one place a microphone exists. So it is the only route that could work there. The vendors cannot close the gap on their side. The Claude Code team has declined to integrate with VS Code's dictation (anthropics/claude-code#43375, closed as not planned). The speech provider API is a proposed API that only ms-vscode.vscode-speech can use, so no other extension can register or consume a session.

## What We Ask For

Either of these would close it:

1. Let the dictation commands target the focused webview input. Deliver the recognised text to the focused element the way terminal dictation does. The workbench would handle the live (partial) text as it does for the Chat view.

2. Finalise a consumer-side speech API. An extension could then request a dictation session on the client and receive `Recognizing` and `Recognized` events to render in its own input.

## What We Do Today

We maintain a small two-part extension with its own recogniser: a UI-kind recorder on the client and a workspace-kind relay. Its only purpose is to give dictation to these panels in a tunnelled window. It duplicates what VS Code already does well. We will retire it as soon as VS Code covers this, and we would be glad to test an Insiders build.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.144.0 (Windows 11), VS Code Speech 0.16.0
- Claude Code extension 2.1.312, Codex extension 26.1021.22027
- Remote Tunnels between two Windows machines

title: MCP tool result: inline Markdown link is rewritten into a broken anchor — the opening `` lands in an unrelated JSON field and the link text/destination becomes ``
body: ### Description - MCP server: built-in GitHub MCP — there is no `mcp.json` and no `mcpServers` entry in user settings, so this is the bundled remote endpoint rather than a locally launched `github-mcp-server`. When a GitHub MCP tool returns content containing an inline Markdown link `[text](url)`, the tool result delivered to the model is corrupted: the link's opening `` is injected into an unrelated JSON field near the start of the result, and the `](url)` part is replaced with a bare ``, so the link text survives but the destination is lost and the JSON is no longer parseable. The corruption is deterministic for a given input and it silently corrupts the data the model reasons over. In the case that surfaced this, the assistant concluded the user's issue body contained a malformed link and asked for a correction that was not needed — the body on GitHub was valid. ### Steps to reproduce 1. With the GitHub MCP server connected, call `issue_read` with `method: "get"`, `owner: "microsoft"`, `repo: "vscode"`, `issue_number: 344880`. 2. Inspect the returned tool result (it exceeds the display limit and is offloaded to a temp file, so read the offloaded file). The issue body contains a single inline link: `[WCAG 2.2, 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#non-text-contrast)`. ### Observed First 130 characters of the result: ```json {"issue":{"assignees":],"author_association":"NONE","body":"### Description\n\nIn Default High Contrast (Dark) Color Theme, the Copilot Chat's WIP mark … ``` `assignees` is `[]` on this issue, and a JSON string value can never contain a bare ``. In the body, the link has become: ```markdown … so it still exceeds the specification of [WCAG 2.2, 1.4.11 if the mark is treated as a meaningful graphical object. ``` So `[` and the link text stay, `](https://…)` is replaced by ``, and the `` half is relocated to `assignees`. ### Determinism The result embeds two copies of the issue (a `content[].text` copy and a `resource.text` copy). Splitting on `}},"method":"get"}`, each copy is corrupted at its own start: | occurrence | offset | |---|---| | `` | 1986 | | `` | 7689 | Both copies show the identical corrupted text at the link (`[WCAG 2.2, 1.4.11`), so the same rewrite is applied to both. The two copies do differ in escaping, which suggests two serialization paths that both run through the same link rewrite: copy 1 keeps `>` as `\u003e`, copy 2 has it as the HTML entity `>`. ### Expected ```json {"issue":{"assignees":[],"author_association":"NONE","body":"… [WCAG 2.2, 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#non-text-contrast) …"}} ``` ### What is not affected | Case | Result | |---|---| | `github-mcp-server-get_file_contents` on `microsoft/vscode/README.md` (13,919 bytes, 80 inline links) | intact — zero `` / `` | | `issue_read` on microsoft/vscode#337085 (body has URLs but no inline `[text](url)`) | intact — `"assignees":["justschen"]` | | Reading a local file containing three inline Markdown links | intact | So the trigger looks specific to `issue_read` results whose body contains an inline Markdown link, rather than to tool output in general. ### Why the open-source GitHub MCP server is not the source - `pkg/sanitize/sanitize.go` in github/github-mcp-server contains **zero** occurrences of `a href`, `linkify`, or `Linkify`. - The repository has **no** Markdown renderer (no goldmark, blackfriday, or equivalent), searched repo-wide. - The only content-preserving path is `func Content(input string) string { return FilterInvisibleCharacters(input) }` — character filtering, which cannot synthesise ``. - `assignees` is an array in the REST payload, so the GitHub API cannot have produced the injected tag either. That points to the client-side Markdown rendering applied to MCP tool results, i.e. the layer between the MCP response and the model. > [!WARNING] > This only covers the open-source implementation. The bundled endpoint is a hosted service and is not verifiable from here, so a defect in that hosted layer cannot be ruled out with the evidence above. ### Open question `issue_read` on github/github-mcp-server#3299 (open, unrelated: long-URL wrapping) shows the same corruption in its first copy — `"assignees":]` with the body's link reduced to `[link` — but its second copy appears intact. That asymmetry is not explained yet: in #3299 the affected link sits inside a fenced code block, while in #344880 it is inline prose. A fenced-code-position dependency in the rewrite would explain it, but that is a hypothesis, not a confirmed cause. > [!NOTE] > Filed against VS Code because the symptom appears in Copilot chat tool results inside VS Code. Only the open-source GitHub MCP server was inspected; the bundled hosted endpoint was not. If the MCP tool-result rendering lives in the agent host rather than the workbench chat contribution, this should be moved. > [!TIP] > Workaround while reading tool results: fetch content through a path that does not post-process tool output — for example `DownloadString` against `raw.githubusercontent.com`, or compare the offloaded temp file against a direct API response before trusting link-containing text. ### Issue Details Item|Value ---|--- Issue Category|Bug Target|Visual Studio Code Repository|Microsoft/vscode VS Code Version|Code 1.144.0 (2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf, 2026-10-27T20:18:03Z) OS Version|Windows_NT arm64 10.0.26300 ### 其他问题数据 [issue-data.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34107781/issue-data.md)

Blobby's color and hat were shared by every window. This lets editor windows and the Agents window each have their own, and removes "on the run".

### Color and hat per window

- Customize Blobby has a new **Apply to** choice (Both Windows | Editor Window | Agents Window) at the top of the Achievements and Color tabs. It resets to Both Windows whenever the page opens and is kept when you switch tabs, so changes apply to both windows by default.
- With Both Windows selected and the windows differing, each card in use is labeled with its window (for example "Wearing in Editor Window"), and choosing a card makes both windows match. With one window selected, only that window's choice is marked and hat previews use that window's color.
- Storage: `chat.vscodePet.color` and `chat.vscodePet.accessory` remain the shared values, so existing appearances carry over. Window overrides (`chat.vscodePet.color.editor` / `.agents` and `chat.vscodePet.accessory.editor` / `.agents`) take precedence and can store "no hat". Applying to both windows writes the shared value and clears the overrides. Resetting achievements also clears custom overrides.

title: Copilot Chat's WIP mark turns focus-ring orange in Default High Contrast (Dark) Color Theme
body:
### Description In Default High Contrast (Dark) Color Theme, the Copilot Chat's WIP mark (the VS Code "Draw" animation) is rendered in `#F38518` — the high-contrast focus-ring color — instead of the product mark color. It reads like a warning/error indicator and does not match the application icon in the title bar. `Preferences: Open User Settings` → `@id:chat.experimental.persistentProgress` does not help: the grayscale filter is explicitly disabled in high-contrast themes, so the option silently has no effect there. ### Root cause - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/widget/chatColors.ts#L130-L133 - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/media/chatWorkingLogo.css#L26-L29 ### Steps to reproduce 1. `Preferences: Color Theme` → `Default High Contrast` 2. `Preferences: Open User Settings` → `@id:chat.experimental.persistentProgress` → `draw` (or `drawMonochrome`) 3. Send a chat request and watch the persistent working-progress indicator ### Expected behavior The mark uses the product / foreground color and the Monochrome variant actually looks monochrome. ### Actual behavior Both variants render in the focus-ring orange `#F38518`. ### Suggested fix - **Primary** (guarantees the brand color)**:** register the token with `hcDark: '#007ACC'`, `hcLight: '#007ACC'` instead of inheriting from `contrastActiveBorder`. This matches the token's own non-high-contrast defaults (`dark` and `light` are already `#007ACC`), so it makes high-contrast behavior consistent rather than introducing a new hardcoded color. `#007ACC` measures 4.66:1 against `#000000` and 4.51:1 against `#FFFFFF`, so it still exceeds the specification of [WCAG 2.2, 1.4.11](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#non-text-contrast) if the mark is treated as a meaningful graphical object. - **Alternative** (if high-contrast themes should stay strictly monochrome)**:** map `hcDark`/`hcLight` to the theme `foreground` (`#FFFFFF` / `#000000`). This forfeits the brand color but keeps the mark from borrowing the focus-ring color. - **In both cases**, also keep the grayscale treatment for the monochrome variant under high contrast by removing the `.hc-black` / `.hc-light` override of `filter: none` (or replacing it with a real monochrome mapping), so `chat.experimental.persistentProgress: "drawMonochrome"` works as documented. > [!NOTE] > The application icon is a blue gradient sampled at `#007ABB`–`#24ACF2`, so a pixel-identical match is not achievable with a single color token. The request is for the token's brand default (`#007ACC`), not an exact match to the icon bitmap. > [!TIP] > Workaround: `Preferences: Open User Settings` → `@id:workbench.colorCustomizations` → `"chat.workingProgressStableIconForeground": "#007ACC"` — `colorCustomizations` outranks theme defaults, so this yields the brand blue in every theme, including high contrast. ### Issue Details Item|Value ---|--- Issue Category|Bug Target|Visual Studio Code Repository|Microsoft/vscode VS Code Version|Code 1.144.0 (2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf, 2026-10-27T20:18:03Z) OS Version|Windows_NT arm64 10.0.26300
