title: Canvases should adapt to the host app and its theme
body:
## Problem

A canvas provider can open the same page in VS Code and the GitHub Copilot app, but it cannot tell which app is presenting it or inherit that app's visual theme. The generated `CanvasHostContext` currently exposes only `capabilities.canvases`.

This leaves providers with poor alternatives:

- ship one generic design that feels foreign in every host;
- infer the host from the user agent, which is brittle;
- use `prefers-color-scheme`, which follows the operating system rather than the selected VS Code theme; or
- require callers to pass appearance through canvas input, which leaks host concerns into the canvas contract and does not update when the user changes themes.

VS Code already has theme context in the canvas editor, but the page rendered in the web contents view does not receive semantic theme information.

## Example

The Topic Atlas canvas should use a modern, dense VS Code dark treatment when opened in VS Code. The same canvas should use a compact Primer-based desktop treatment in the GitHub Copilot app. Content, state, actions, and canvas identity should remain the same.

## Expected outcome

Canvas providers have a supported way to:

- identify the presenting host application;
- style against semantic host colors rather than copying fixed palettes;
- follow relevant host theme changes without reopening the canvas; and
- fall back predictably when a host does not provide presentation context.

The contract should be sufficient for one canvas implementation to feel native in multiple hosts without relying on user-agent detection or caller-supplied appearance settings.

## Acceptance criteria

- The same canvas provider can render distinct app-native treatments in VS Code and the GitHub Copilot app without changing its open input.
- A VS Code canvas can follow the active VS Code color theme, including dark and light changes.
- Presentation context uses documented, semantic values with a safe fallback.
- Host identity and theme propagation have contract and integration coverage.

title: test: fail unit test suites that leak command, menu or keybinding registrations
body:
Adds a unit test harness check that fails any top-level suite which leaves a different set of commands, menu items or keybindings registered than it started with.

## Why

All test files in a unit test run share one page, so a registration that a suite doesn't dispose changes the behavior of every suite that runs after it. PR CI runs per-area file sets with `--runList` and `--workers 4`, while the official build runs every file in one page. A leak can therefore pass PR CI and still break `main`. That happened with #344654: `chatViewModeActions.test` called `registerChatActions()` in `suiteSetup` and never unregistered `workbench.action.chat.open`, which broke `ChatTipService` in every official unit test job until #344844 fixed it.

This check makes such a leak fail in the leaking suite itself, in whatever file set it runs, PR CI included.

## How

- `src/vs/platform/actions/test/common/registryLeakCheck.ts`: `installRegistryLeakCheck(mocha.suite)` adds two hooks to every top-level suite:
  - a `suiteSetup` hook, registered before the suite's own hooks, that snapshots `CommandsRegistry`, `MenuRegistry` (commands and items for every `MenuId`) and `KeybindingsRegistry`
  - a `suiteTeardown` hook, registered after them, so it runs after the suite's own cleanup. It fails with the list of registered, replaced or unregistered entries.
- `test/unit/browser/renderer.html` and `test/unit/electron/renderer.js` install it before loading the test modules.
- Registrations made while modules load are part of the baseline, so only registrations made by a suite's hooks and tests count.
- The 8 suites that leak today are in `knownLeakingSuites`, so this lands green. They should be fixed separately and removed from that list:
  - `AgentSessionsActions`
  - `Chat code-block action telemetry`
  - `ChatMcpAuthenticationContentPart`
  - `Edit session sync`
  - `ExtHostLanguageFeatureCommands`
  - `Inline chat zone widget — menu contributions`
  - `RetryChatAction`
  - `Sessions - Layout Actions`

## Validation

- **Red, with #344844 reverted, running only `chatViewModeActions.test.ts`:** the check fails `Chat View Mode` in both the Chromium and Electron runners, starting with `registered command 'workbench.action.chat.open'`.
- **Green, with #344844:** 19 passing in Chromium and 20 in Electron.
- **Full Chromium suite** (all files in one page): 49,501 passing. Before the allowlist, the check failed only the 8 suites listed above. The one other failure was the unrelated `Extensions viewlet notification layout` network error, which also fails on this machine without the change. The 8 allowlisted files pass together (129 passing).
- **Full Electron suite with `--workers 4`:** 0 leak-check failures. The 167 failures on this machine are the same local rendering timeouts (`MultiEditorTabsControl`, `ChatListRenderer` and others) that also occur without the change.
- **Cost:** one check (two snapshots plus the diff) takes about 0.9 ms at full registry size (1,281 commands, 171 menus, 604 keybindings). Across 2,708 top-level suites that's about 2.5 s per full run, which is under 0.5% of an 11 min Chromium run.
- eslint is clean, and tsc reports no errors in `platform/actions`.

## Not covered

- Registries other than commands, menus and keybindings, for example editor contributions or configuration.
- Leaks between nested suites in the same file.
- Non-registry leaks such as global CSS (see #344831) or focus order (#344605).

## Overlap with open drafts (checked Oct 29 with `git merge-tree`)

- **#342237 (parallel workers), #344229 (repeat added tests) and #343097 (worker benchmark experiment):** this PR adds no new conflicting files with any of them. They already conflict with `main` in `test/unit/*` and the workflows. The only overlap is in #343097's `renderer.html` bootstrap block, which already conflicts with `main` there, so its rebase picks up these two lines.
- **Repeats:** #344229's `--repeat`, and `--rerun-failed-files` on `main`, run each attempt in a fresh window, process or browser. Every attempt gets fresh registries and its own snapshots, so a repeated suite can't trip the check because of an earlier attempt.

title: Coordinate remote inventory checks for local uninstall batches
body:
Fixes #344862.

Avoid repeated remote inventory reads during local uninstall batches while preserving dependency consistency through physical deletion against participating VS Code-managed writers. Reserve one inventory per batch, durably fence retries/recovery, and await remote release plus local acknowledgement. Older backends retain ordered checks.

Keep downloads and post-install work outside the global SQL transaction. Drain existing task waits before acquiring it; recheck inventory and reservations before publication. Retain compatible in-flight reads, same-profile removal batching, and the unrelated AI/English inventory-read shortcuts.

### How to test

- Run the coordinator, native install concurrency, profile scanner, uninstall batching, IPC, and coordinated-uninstall tests, plus the AI-customization and localization contribution tests.
- In a remote workspace, uninstall local batches of 1, 3, and 20. Check dependency rejection, installs attempted during reservation, interrupted recovery, and a stalled download alongside independent reads/installs.

Validation: 131 native/common tests, 27 renderer tests, six source-built SSH consistency controls, client typecheck, and targeted lint passed. The stalled-download regression fails on the previous PR head and passes here.

Thirty-six matched warm timings (three samples per cell, 100 remote fixtures, English UI): three-item medians changed 111.6→120.9 ms on loopback and 260.5→253.4 ms with 50 ms added egress delay versus the previous head. This includes a small loopback cost; no universal speedup is claimed. Timings include physical deletion and awaited release/acknowledgement.

Single-item overhead versus upstream remains outside this PR's scope. Draft for design/performance review. Testing bypasses the proprietary Remote SSH resolver; non-English UI performance is unqualified. Recovery fails closed and can cancel a competing operation.

title: Add an option to add worktree to workspace
body: We can open a worktree in either the current window or in a new window, but if we want to add it to the current workspace we have to go to File --> Add Folder to Workspace... --> navigate your file system to find the workspace to select it. It would be very nice to have this option here instead so it's easier to add it to the current workspace. It also makes intuitive sense to have the option there: Besides, when creating a new worktree it would be nice if VSCode asked you whether you want to open it in the current window or in a new window or add it to the current workspace or leave it there, since that's the logical next step to take when you create a new worktree.

## Summary

Installed plugin details currently lose marketplace source metadata that is available while browsing. This change preserves trustworthy GitHub repository provenance and surfaces it alongside the installed version and location.

title: Avoid serial remote inventory reads for each local extension in an uninstall batch
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested with `--disable-extensions`; the reproduction exercises extension management using installed fixtures.

- VS Code Version: source-built Code - OSS 1.145.0, commit `6f83f69aad09f4dfd85ae585e8b6835a196d410d` (latest Insiders not tested).
- OS Version: macOS arm64 client and Linux server over an SSH tunnel; exact OS release versions were not recorded. The proprietary Remote SSH resolver was not exercised.

In a remote window, removing a local extension batch fetches the full remote user-extension inventory once per local item. These requests run serially before local removal, so their round-trip cost grows with the batch size.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a remote workspace with local and remote extensions installed.
2. Uninstall a local extension pack and its members, or submit a multi-extension local uninstall batch.
3. Inspect the remote `getInstalled(ExtensionType.User)` requests made by the dependency guard before local removal starts.

**Actual:** each local item triggers another complete remote inventory request.

**Expected:** local uninstall batches avoid repeated remote inventory work while dependency validation remains consistent through local deletion against participating VS Code-managed installs, updates, and removals.

The scope is batch uninstall performance and that consistency guarantee. Eliminating all coordination overhead for single-item removal is outside this issue's acceptance criteria.

The per-item read is in [`uninstallInServer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6f83f69aad09f4dfd85ae585e8b6835a196d410d/src/vs/workbench/services/extensionManagement/common/extensionManagementService.ts#L256-L269). A reused snapshot or final recheck alone does not protect the interval before local deletion.

This concerns repeated inventory work, separate from the mixed local/remote removal ordering reported in #343168.

title: sanity: run UI tests without experiment treatments
body:
@dmitrivMS asked on #344714 whether sanity should run with experiment treatments disabled. Until now sanity didn't turn them off anywhere, so a treatment going live could fail sanity on a build that had already passed. That happened today: `chat.agentHost.cloudSandbox.enabled` made every `server-web-*` test fail with `File not found …/github-authentication/dist/browser/extension.js`. The product gap behind that failure is tracked in #344852 and stays open. This PR only makes sanity deterministic.

## Change (test-only)

- **Desktop and WSL desktop** launches pass `--disable-experiments`.
- **Every Playwright page**, browser and Electron, goes through `TestContext.getPage`, which now aborts requests to the ExP service (`*.exp-tas.com`). A browser workbench has no `--disable-experiments` equivalent: its environment service always returns `false` for `disableExperiments`. So for server-web, dev tunnel and WSL web, blocking the request is the only switch. Without assignments, the workbench uses each setting's default.

## Validation (Windows, insider `ea8056df9f0`)

- **`server-web-win32-x64`:** fails on `main` right now with the #344852 signature. With this change it passes. The log shows `https://default.exp-tas.com/vscode/ab net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`.
- **`desktop-win32-x64-archive`:** launches with `--disable-experiments`, makes no ExP request, and runs the UI steps. Locally it later stops at the Marketplace search, because this machine's policy forces a private marketplace. That's unrelated to this change.
- `tsc` for `test/sanity` and eslint on the touched files are clean.

## Overlap

I checked this with `git merge-tree` against #337603, #338607, #342405 and #342659. This PR adds no new conflicts: each of them has the same conflicts against `main` alone, and #342659 merges cleanly. #337603 rewrites `testDesktopApp` in `desktop.test.ts`, so if it lands first, this PR's one-line `--disable-experiments` change in that function needs a trivial rebase.

title: agentHost: preserve MCP App tool-result _meta for restored cards
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #343243

Agent Host rebuilt MCP App `ui/notifications/tool-result` notifications from session state without the server's result `_meta`. App-only data (e.g. `_meta.flint.board` in the issue) was lost when a card was reconstructed, including after reopening a session or restarting.

### Changes
- The Copilot runtime now reports the verbatim MCP `CallToolResult._meta` on `tool.execution_complete` as `result.mcpResultMeta`, for MCP App tools only (github/copilot-agent-runtime#30458). It is separate from the IFC-only `mcpMeta`.
- Adds `resultMetadata?: Record<string, unknown>` to AHP `ToolCallResult`, mirroring MCP `CallToolResult._meta` the same way `structuredContent` mirrors `structuredContent`. The canonical protocol change is microsoft/agent-host-protocol#549; the synced types here are updated to match. The protocol reducer, result confirmation (`agentSideEffects`), and conversation import validation carry it like `structuredContent`.
- `copilotAgentSession.ts` (live completion) and `mapSessionEvents.ts` (history replay) set `resultMetadata` from the runtime's `mcpResultMeta`. Host-owned tool-call `_meta` (`ui`, `toolKind`, ...) is untouched.
- `stateToProgressAdapter.ts` (`toMcpCallToolResult`) rebuilds `resultMetadata` as the MCP result `_meta` for completed tools only. Metadata-only (`content: []`) and error results count as real results.
- Model-facing conversion (`agentHostMcpAppToolsService._convertResult`) is unchanged and does not include result `_meta`.
- The pinned `@github/copilot-sdk` does not declare `mcpResultMeta` yet, so `getSdkMcpResultMeta` reads it through a narrow cast (TODO to remove after the SDK bump). With an older runtime the field is absent and behavior is unchanged.

### How to test
1. Run a runtime/SDK build that includes github/copilot-agent-runtime#30458.
2. Add an MCP App server whose tool result carries `_meta`. The ext-apps `basic-server-vanillajs` example with a per-call `_meta.example.verificationToken` works; it displays the received token.
3. In an Agent Host chat, have the model call the tool. The card shows the token. Reopen the session and restart VS Code: the same token is shown. **Get Server Time** shows a new one.

### Validation
- `scripts/test.bat --run` on agentMetaReaders, agentHostCreateSessionImportMeta, copilotAgentSession, mapSessionEvents, reducers, agentSideEffects, stateToProgressAdapter, and agentHostMcpAppToolsService tests: 2334 passing.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passes against the pinned SDK, and against a local SDK that declares the field.
- `npm run eslint` on the changed files: clean.
- Manual end to end with a local runtime build and the example above: live, reopened, and cold-restarted cards all received the original token.

title: Compare Browse Customizations loading progress treatments
body:
## Goal

Compare two loading-progress treatments for **Browse Customizations** and produce matched video evidence so the team can choose between them.

The current source-aware treatment reports progress such as **“Refreshing customizations… 4 of 7 sources refreshed.”** Team feedback questions whether the source count is meaningful because most users do not configure or understand the underlying sources. An alternative is a generic progress bar that communicates ongoing work without exposing source implementation details.

## Approaches to Prototype

### Option A: Generic progress bar

Show an indeterminate progress bar while Browse Customizations is refreshing. Do not expose source names or counts.

### Option B: Source-count progress

Show explicit textual progress such as **“Refreshing customizations… 4 of 7 sources refreshed.”** Preserve the current source-aware feedback.

## Investigation

- Identify the actual refresh lifecycle and whether progress is determinate, monotonic, and trustworthy.
- Evaluate whether source counts communicate useful user-facing information or leak an implementation detail.
- Compare perceived responsiveness, visual stability, screen-reader behavior, reduced-motion behavior, and behavior during fast, slow, partial, failed, and repeated refreshes.
- Keep all behavior identical except for the progress treatment so the comparison isolates this decision.
- Do not select or ship a winner before review.

## Required Decision Evidence

Produce two matched videos using the same build, viewport, theme, data, source configuration, network/loading conditions, timing, crop, and interaction sequence:

| Option A: Generic progress bar | Option B: Source-count progress |
| --- | --- |
| _Attach video here_ | _Attach video here_ |

Each video must show refresh start, intermediate loading, incremental result behavior if present, and completion. Include a short accessibility and trade-off summary beneath the videos, then request a team choice between A and B.

## Done When

- Both approaches are implemented as reviewable prototypes without unrelated changes.
- The two matched videos are available side by side in this issue.
- Differences, accessibility implications, and technical constraints are documented.
- The team can choose an option based on equivalent visual evidence.

_Context captured from a team discussion comparing source-count messaging with a generic progress bar._

title: Fix Quick Pick item tooltip clipping and relayout (#174900)
body:
🤖 This PR was prepared by an AI agent (GitHub Copilot) for review by @sbatten.

Fixes #174900

## Problem

Quick Pick item tooltips (`IQuickPickItem.tooltip`) were laid out badly, and it is broader than images:

- **Modern UI (default).** The tooltip's context view was `position: absolute` inside `.quick-input-widget`, which has `overflow: hidden`. The tooltip was clipped and only the pointer sliver showed. When Tab focused a link inside it, the widget's hidden overflow scrolled and pushed the input and rows out of view.
- **Modern UI off.** The widget is still the containing block, so a side tooltip shrink-wrapped to a ~79 px column pinned to the top, with its pointer detached from the row. In a short window, keyboard invocation showed nothing.
- **Delayed content (images).** `HoverWidget` kept its last fallback side, so the hover never returned to the requested side. It compared the unclamped height against the window for the vertical fallback, and it kept inline pointer offsets from the previous axis. After an image loaded, the pointer ended up inside the hover.

## Changes

- `QuickInputList` owns a viewport-sized host (`.quick-input-list-hover-host`: `position: fixed; inset: 0; pointer-events: none`, with `pointer-events: auto` on its `.context-view` child) inside the list, and passes it as the item hover's `container`. The hover service keeps its normal absolute context view, so **the hover API and `HoverService` are unchanged from `main`**. The hover stays a DOM descendant of the widget, so the focus tracker and Tab into the tooltip behave as before, while the widget's `overflow: hidden` and size no longer affect it. (An earlier revision of this PR added a public `useFixedPosition` hover option instead; it was replaced to keep this Quick Input-specific concern out of the hover API.)
- `QuickInputController` *settles* the entrance animation, so the widget stops being a containing block for the fixed-position host (`animation: none; will-change: auto` via `quick-input-widget-motion-settled`).
  - It settles when `quick-input-widget-open` ends, or right before an item tooltip is measured.
  - The marker is removed only on a hidden → visible `show()`. Tooltip toggles and visible controller replacement don't replay the animation, and the close animation is kept (`:not(.quick-input-widget-closing)`).
- `HoverWidget.layout()`:
  - re-starts from the requested position on every layout;
  - uses `min(height, maxHeight)` for the ABOVE/BELOW fallback;
  - clamps LEFT/RIGHT hovers vertically into the window (not when `forcePosition` is set);
  - clears stale inline pointer `top`/`left` before positioning;
  - only applies the LEFT branch's trailing bounds check while the hover is still LEFT, so a BELOW fallback for a LEFT-requested hover is no longer overwritten with RIGHT (pre-existing on `main`, made persistent by the per-layout reset; found by Copilot review).
- `QuickInputList` dismisses the item hover when the list has moved since it was shown (window resize, alignment change, re-centring), since a viewport-positioned hover no longer follows the picker; relayouts in place keep it (found by Copilot review).

No image-load callback is added: markdown hovers already re-layout when their content changes.

## Tests

The tests run under `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --run src/vs/platform/hover/test/browser/hoverService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/quickinput/test/browser/quickinput.test.ts --browser chromium`:
- **With this change:** 111 passing.
- **Without the production changes:** the 7 new tests fail on behavioural assertions, not setup.
- **Without only the pointer-offset reset:** the fallback test fails on the stale pointer position.

New tests:

- `HoverService` (`showInstantHover`):
  - the fallback chain re-evaluates as content changes, including computed pointer placement;
  - the clamped vertical fallback;
  - a tall side hover stays in the window with the pointer on the target;
  - an ABOVE-requested hover re-evaluates ABOVE → BELOW → ABOVE (fails on `main`, where it stays BELOW);
  - a LEFT-requested hover re-evaluates LEFT → RIGHT → BELOW and back (fails on `main` and without the LEFT guard).
- `QuickInput item hover layout` uses a real controller, real `HoverService` and real CSS, with Modern UI + motion on and frosted glass off. It checks:
  - the item hover renders in an absolute context view that is a direct child of the viewport-sized host inside the list, and only the hover receives pointer events (fails on the previous `useFixedPosition` revision);
  - geometry during and after the open animation;
  - no animation replay when tooltips are hidden or replaced, fail to show, or lose their items;
  - a visible picker → picker → input box replacement keeps the widget settled, the close animation runs, and a new show animates;
  - the item hover is dismissed when the picker moves and kept when it is relaid out in place.

## Manual verification

Same base commit, unfixed vs fixed. A deterministic one-item Quick Pick with text tooltips, and an image tooltip whose request is held for 1.5 s:

- **macOS desktop (Code OSS dev):**
  - mouse and Ctrl+Space;
  - Modern UI on/off and frosted glass on/off;
  - windows of 1400×900, 1000×700, 760×520 and 700×500;
  - the picker dragged to the right edge, so only LEFT fits.

  The tooltip is visible in every sampled frame (vs 0 before in Modern UI), stays inside the window, and has 0 px pointer error. After the image loads it re-lays out exactly once, with no oscillation.
- **Keyboard:** Ctrl+Space → Tab → tooltip → link → Escape gives the same focus order and dismissal as before. The focused tooltip is now visible.
- **Web** (code-server + Chromium): same before/after result for the default-setting scenarios.
- **Not verified:** Windows/Linux desktop and high-contrast themes.

## Notes

- `HoverWidget` geometry changes affect all workbench hovers. They only matter when a hover re-lays out, overflows the window vertically, or changes axis.
- These open PRs touch nearby code and may need a trivial rebase:
  - #316992, the same reset block in `HoverWidget.layout()`;
  - #332608, Quick Input.

title: Seti icon theme: no file icon for PowerPoint files (.pptx/.pptm/.potx/.pps)
body:
# [Seti icon theme] No file icon for PowerPoint files (.pptx, .pptm, .potx, .pps)

The default **Seti** icon theme has file-extension mappings and glyphs for Word and Excel files, but **nothing for any PowerPoint file type**. As a result, `.pptx` / `.pptm` / `.potx` / `.pps` files render the generic file icon in the Explorer and in editor tabs, while `.docx` / `.xlsx` get themed icons.

## Evidence

From `resources/app/extensions/theme-seti/icons/vs-seti-icon-theme.json` (VS Code 1.141.1 stable, Linux x64):

`fileExtensions` mappings:

| Key | Maps to |
| --- | --- |
| `doc`, `docx` | `_word` |
| `xls`, `xlsx` | `_xls` |
| `ppt`, `pptx`, `pptm`, `potx`, `pps` | *(absent)* |

Additionally, `iconDefinitions` contains **no** `_powerpoint` entry among its 383 icons — so this is not just a missing mapping; the theme has no PowerPoint glyph at all.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use the default Seti icon theme.
2. Create three files: `a.docx`, `a.xlsx`, `a.pptx` (content is irrelevant).
3. Look at the Explorer / editor tabs.

ⓘ `a.docx` shows the Word icon, `a.xlsx` shows the Excel icon, `a.pptx` shows the generic file icon.

## Expected behavior

PowerPoint file types get an icon consistent with the existing Word/Excel treatment.

## Fix notes

Adding the `fileExtensions` mappings alone will not be enough — a PowerPoint glyph also needs to be added to the theme (Seti font + `iconDefinitions`), analogous to `_word` / `_xls` (incl. `_light` variants).

## Versions

- VS Code: 1.141.1 (stable)
- OS: Linux x64 (Ubuntu, GNOME/Wayland)

The agent host's BYOK proxy turns renderer LM API results into OpenAI Responses payloads for the Copilot runtime. It always set `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` to `0`. The runtime treats a non-null `cached_tokens` as provider-reported cache details, so every BYOK call was recorded as a confirmed cache miss. title: build: fail a stuck Windows ESRP signing session fast
body:
Fails a stuck Windows ESRP signing session in about 20 minutes instead of letting it hold the sign job until its 90 minute limit.

## Evidence

- **What happens:** [490380](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=490380) `Windows (ARM64) - Sign` › `✍️ Codesign`. ESRP signed and replaced every file except one within 3 minutes (`1 file(s) remaining, FileIds: 1a78000a-…` at 18:43 UTC). It then polled that operation's status every 10 s for 83 minutes, until the job's 90 minute limit canceled it. A stage retry passed.
- **Why ESRP doesn't give up on its own:** `sign.ts` passes `-t 120`, and the ESRP CLI logs `SessionTimeoutMinutes: 120`. That's longer than the Windows sign job's `timeoutInMinutes: 90`, so ESRP's own timeout can never fire.
- **How long a normal session waits:** across 115 sampled Windows Codesign runs in def 111 over 30 days (main and release, scheduled, batched and manual), the longest wait without the remaining count changing was **5.3 min** (p50 1.0, p95 3.2, p99 5.3). Outside that sample, the stragglers were:
  - official [484683](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=484683): last file took 9 min, then finished
  - 486779: last file took 37 min, then finished
  - 490380: last file never finished
  - official 484798: hit the job limit on both arches

## Change

All in `build/azure-pipelines/common/sign.ts`, and only for `sign-windows` and `sign-windows-appx`. The darwin, linux, pgp and nuget paths are unchanged.

- **Stall guard:** ESRP's output is mirrored and tracked. `N file(s) remaining` changes and `Signed file:` lines count as progress, and status polling doesn't. If ESRP has pending operations and none completes for **20 minutes** (`VSCODE_ESRP_STALL_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` overrides it), the ESRP process tree is killed and the step fails with:
  `ESRP signing stalled: N file(s) still pending after 20 minutes without progress (FileIds: …). Retry the stage, not this step: files signed so far were replaced in place.`
- **20 minutes** is about 4x the longest normal wait. A fresh stage costs about 15 to 20 minutes, so waiting longer than that on one operation doesn't pay off.
- **ESRP session timeout for Windows signing:** lowered from 120 to 60 minutes, so ESRP's own timeout can also fire within the job limit. The longest successful Windows Codesign in 30 days took 52 minutes.
- **No resubmit:** ESRP replaces each file as soon as it's signed, and `sign-windows` signs with `/as` (append). Re-running the session would add a second signature to every file it already signed. A stage retry starts from unsigned artifacts, so it's clean.
- `sign-win32.ts` (Inno Setup's signing hook) now awaits `main`, since the Windows path is async.

## Validation

- `build/lib/test/esrpStallGuard.test.ts`, 8 tests:
  - parsing, including split chunks and CRLF
  - status polling doesn't count as progress
  - an unchanged count doesn't count as progress
  - the env override
  - a session that finishes
  - a failed session's exit code
  - a slow session that keeps making progress isn't stopped
  - a session stuck on its last operation is stopped promptly
- Def 111 with official parameters (only Publish and Release off):
  - **Forced stall:** [490442](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=490442) ran on a throwaway branch that sets `VSCODE_ESRP_STALL_TIMEOUT_MINUTES: "0.5"`.
    - **Windows ARM64:** a real ESRP session got to `3 file(s) remaining`, made no progress for 36 s, and the guard killed it. `✍️ Codesign` failed after **2.4 min**, and the pipeline showed: `ESRP signing stalled: 3 file(s) still pending after 0.5 minutes without progress (FileIds: …). Retry the stage, not this step: …`.
    - **Windows x64:** its longest gap was 30.3 s, so the guard didn't trip and the job passed. Its Inno Setup signing (`sign-win32.ts`, now `await`ed) signed both setups.
    - I canceled the run once the Windows Sign jobs had finished.
  - **Normal path:** [490441](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=490441) on this head.
    - Windows ARM64 and x64 `✍️ Codesign` passed, including setup signing.
    - Quality passed, including the build-script tests, compile and hygiene.
    - The only failures are 1 unit test per job, `ChatTipService`. That's today's break on `main` from #344654, fixed by #344844, and it's unrelated to this change.
> Authored with Copilot

title: Allow BYOK models to declare tool search capability
body:
## Description

Adds an optional per-model `toolSearch` field to the BYOK models config (`chatLanguageModels.json`), letting `customendpoint` models explicitly declare support for client-executed Responses API tool search.

Fixes #334424

### Semantics (three-state)

- `"toolSearch": true` — explicitly enable the tool-search path, overriding the model-id heuristic
- `"toolSearch": false` — explicitly disable it, even if the model id/family would otherwise match the heuristic
- omitted — preserve current behavior (fall back to `modelSupportsToolSearch(...)`)

### What the declaration does

The field flows through the BYOK provider → language model metadata → agent host bridge, so a declared model:

- skips the 128-tool `capBridgeTools` cap in the BYOK proxy (`byokLmProxyService`)
- gets tool-search deferral enabled in agent host sessions (`copilotSessionLauncher` gate now honors the BYOK declaration in addition to the id heuristic)

This addresses the root cause of third-party models failing with >128 tools (e.g. DeepSeek's 502 `单次 tools 请求最多支持 128 个 functions`) without family aliasing, which changes the whole prompt/tool profile.

### Example

```json
[
  {
    "vendor": "customendpoint",
    "apiKey": "${input:chat.lm.secret.example}",
    "models": [
      {
        "id": "my-responses-model",
        "name": "My Responses Model",
        "url": "https://example.com/v1/responses",
        "apiType": "responses",
        "toolCalling": true,
        "toolSearch": true,
        "vision": false,
        "maxInputTokens": 200000,
        "maxOutputTokens": 32000
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

## How to test

- Unit tests: `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokLmProxyService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostByokLmHandler.test.ts`
- Extension tests: `cd extensions/copilot && npx vitest run src/extension/byok/common/test/byokProvider.spec.ts src/extension/byok/vscode-node/test/customEndpointProvider.spec.ts`
- Integration test (real bundled copilot-runtime): `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/copilotByokToolSearch.integrationTest.ts` — declared model is uncapped at 130 tools, undeclared model is capped at 128, runtime defers to 1 tool with search on
- Manual: configure a `customendpoint` model with `apiType: "responses"` and `"toolSearch": true`, enable >128 tools (e.g. via MCP servers), and run an agent session — the request no longer fails with the 128-function limit and tools are deferred

title: Engineering - retry and bound node-gyp header installs
body:
Retries and bounds the two `node-gyp install` calls in `build/npm/preinstall.ts`, so one failed or stalled header download doesn't fail the dependency install. Follow-up to #344728 (t55).

## Why

Every root `npm ci` runs `preinstall.ts`, which runs `node-gyp install --dist-url` twice with no retry and no deadline:
- the Electron 43.8.3 headers from electronjs.org (root `.npmrc`)
- the Node.js 24.22.1 headers from nodejs.org (`remote/.npmrc`)

During the Oct 28 nodejs.org degradation from the 1ES agents, this failed Alpine in the 11:00 insider [490207](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=490207) with `gyp ERR! Completion callback never invoked`. It needed a stage retry.

Exposure across the last 13 scheduled insiders:
- 237 header downloads (176 from electronjs.org, 61 from nodejs.org).
- `WindowsAPIScan` downloads them in every build.
- After a lockfile change, up to 15 jobs install them (488681 had 15, 489779 had 13).

## Change

- New `build/npm/nodeGypHeaders.ts`, next to `preinstall.ts` so the cloud sandbox install test fixture can copy it,, with `installNodeGypHeaders(nodeGypScript, distUrl, target)`:
  - It runs node-gyp's `bin/node-gyp.js` through the current Node.js, so it needs no shell, and the deadline kills node-gyp itself.
  - Each attempt has a 5 min deadline. It retries twice, after 10 s and 30 s.
  - The error names the target, the URL and the attempt.

title: Copilot CLI session listing at startup exhausts the system file table (ENFILE) with a large ~/.copilot/session-state
body:
### Description

Related: #327021 covers the repeated full re-walk and the resulting slowness. This issue is about a distinct consequence of the same code path: unbounded file-descriptor usage at cold start, which breaks process spawning in the extension host and, with several windows, the whole machine. #331853 fixed the same unbounded `Promise.all` pattern in prompt discovery; the CLI session listing has the same problem.

## Environment

- VS Code Insiders 1.145.0-insider, Electron 43.8.3, macOS (Darwin 27.2.0), `kern.maxfiles` 122,880, `kern.maxfilesperproc` 61,440
- GitHub Copilot Chat 0.73.2026102802 (built-in, `extensions/copilot`), bundling `@github/copilot` SDK 1.0.73
- `~/.copilot/session-state` with 42,329 sessions (19 GB), produced by `copilot -p` batch runs

## Symptom

Cold start with five restored windows drives system-wide open files from ~10,500 to a peak of 122,477 (`sysctl kern.num_files`) within about 40 s, then back to ~11,000. While the table is full:

- every window's `exthost.log` shows `Error: spawn .../ripgrep/bin/rg ENFILE` (1 to 15 per window)
- the built-in git extension's `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` takes 1.5 to 3.4 s instead of ~50 ms
- `GitHub.copilot-chat` log: `[CopilotCLIChatSessionContentProvider] listSessions took` 92,000 to 137,000 ms per window
- window 1 also logged `spawn EBADF` (extension host, and Copilot Chat's `ExternalIngestIndex::reconcileDbFiles`), and the ESLint extension failed to start its server in that window with `couldn't create connection to server` (microsoft/vscode-eslint#2136). Restart ESLint Server does not recover; the window needs a reload.

An `lsof` capture of one extension host at the peak showed 19,985 `events.jsonl` files from `~/.copilot/session-state` open at the same instant (20,043 of its 20,086 descriptors). Five windows doing this concurrently overflow the kernel table.

After pruning to 449 sessions the peak was 11,724 files with no ENFILE, but `listSessions` still took 7 to 12 s per window, so the per-session cost is significant even at modest counts.

## Root cause

1. The extension activates on `onChatSession:copilotcli` in every window and immediately lists all CLI sessions (`provideChatSessionItems` in `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/vscode-node/copilotCLIChatSessions.ts`).
2. `_getAllSessions` in `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/copilotcli/node/copilotcliSessionService.ts` calls `sessionManager.listSessions()` with no arguments. The SDK supports a `metadataLimit` option that bounds how many sessions get their metadata read; without it every session is examined.
3. Inside the SDK, `listSessions` runs an unbounded `Promise.all` over every session directory and per session reads `workspace.yaml`, reads `events.jsonl` for the first user message (summary), and reads `events.jsonl` again for detached-status detection. All of those file handles are open simultaneously. Filed against the SDK as github/copilot-cli#5282.
4. The extension then does another unbounded `Promise.all(sessions.map(toChatSessionItem))` with git-based badge and metadata work per session.
5. `github.copilot.chat.cli.lazyLoadSessionItem.enabled` (default true, deprecated) only skips `buildChanges`; it does not affect the SDK reads.

### Why spawns fail before the system table is full

On macOS `uv_spawn` returns `EBADF` as soon as the stdio pipe descriptors it creates for the child are numbered above 10239, regardless of `ulimit -n` or `kern.maxfilesperproc` (libuv/libuv#5204, attributed to Apple libc). So any extension host holding more than about 10,000 descriptors cannot fork or spawn anything until the listing finishes. With a store above ~10k sessions this hits every extension in that window that starts a child process (ESLint server, ripgrep, git, language servers), even on a single window and even with a large system file table. The ENFILE above is the additional effect of several windows doing it at once.

## Repro

```bash
cd ~/.copilot/session-state
for i in $(seq 1 20000); do d=$(uuidgen | tr A-Z a-z); mkdir "$d"
  printf 'id: %s\ncwd: /tmp\ncreated_at: 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z\nupdated_at: 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z\n' "$d" > "$d/workspace.yaml"
  printf '{"type":"session.start","data":{"sessionId":"%s"}}\n{"type":"user.message","data":{"content":"hello"}}\n' "$d" > "$d/events.jsonl"
done
```

Open a window with Copilot Chat signed in and the ESLint extension installed, quit, relaunch, and run `while true; do sysctl -n kern.num_files; sleep 0.5; done` during startup. Watch `lsof -p <extension host pid> | grep -c events.jsonl` climb past 10,000 and the ESLint output channel report `spawn EBADF`. With 3 to 5 restored windows the system table also overflows (ENFILE).

## Proposed fix

- Pass `metadataLimit` (for example the number of items the Agent Sessions view can show) to `listSessions`, and page or lazily resolve the rest on demand.
- List once per machine, not once per window: share the result through the agent host or a cache keyed on the directory mtime, instead of every extension host walking the store at activation.
- Bound concurrency in `toChatSessionItem` (a small worker pool) so git and file work is not fanned out over every session at once.
- Do not list sessions at all until the Agent Sessions view is actually shown.

title: agentHost: strip subagent chat selectors in session resolution and guard post-shutdown config syncs
body:
Fixes #344272

## Summary

While the unexpected deletion of graduated provisional sessions and their forks in #344272 was fixed by #343104, two remaining issues in #344272 still occur on `main`:

1. **Subagent chat editor query parameters (`?subagentChatResource=...`) poison session resolution and `sessions_v2`:**
   - When opening a subagent chat editor (`agent-host-copilotcli:/<id>?subagentChatResource=ahp-chat%3A%2F...#<chatId>`), `AgentHostConnectionsService.resolveSessionResourceIdentity` only stripped `fragment` and left `?subagentChatResource=...` on the URI.
   - This missed the advertised `ahp-session:/<id>` record in `_backendSessions` and synthesized a bogus `copilotcli:/<id>?subagentChatResource=...` backend session URI.
   - Workbench contributors subscribing to `StateComponents.Session` with that URI caused the Agent Host to inspect `agentSessionData/<id>/session.db` (keyed by path ID alone), treat the query-carrying URI as native, and register a phantom `copilotcli:/<id>?subagentChatResource=...` row in `sessions_v2`. If the parent session was later deleted, restoring or reloading failed permanently with `Provider copilotcli is not ready to open copilotcli:/<id>?subagentChatResource=...` instead of `Session was explicitly deleted`.

2. **Post-shutdown configuration updates during session/chat disposal:**
   - During `disposeChat` / `disposeSession`, `_deleteSdkSession` destroys the SDK session before the `CopilotAgentSession` wrapper is disposed. Concurrent root or chat config updates (`permissionMode`, `sandboxConfig`, `imageGeneration`, `shellInitScripts`) still invoked `session.rpc.options.update` against the shut-down SDK session, logging `Failed to apply SDK sandboxConfig` / `Session not found` errors.

## Changes

- **`AgentHostConnectionsService` ([agentHostConnectionsService.ts](src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/agentHostConnectionsService.ts)):**
  - Strip the workbench `subagentChatResource` query selector (in addition to `fragment`) when normalizing session resources unless the exact query-bearing URI was explicitly advertised by the host.
- **`AgentService` & `CopilotAgent` ([agentService.ts](src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts), [copilotAgent.ts](src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts)):**
  - Check both `<provider>:/<id>` and `ahp-session:/<id>` suppression/tombstones in `_isSessionSuppressed` for standard-URI providers so deleted sessions consistently report `Session was explicitly deleted` across legacy, standard, or previously poisoned URIs.
  - Decline `ensureChatAdopted`, `getChatMetadata`, and `_readDefaultChatBackingProviderData` for session URIs carrying an `authority`, `query`, or `fragment` so they cannot read another session's `session.db` or register phantom `sessions_v2` entries.
- **`CopilotAgentSession` & `CopilotSessionSandbox` ([copilotAgentSession.ts](src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts), [copilotSessionSandbox.ts](src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionSandbox.ts), [copilotSessionLauncher.ts](src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts)):**
  - Skip background permission, sandbox, image-generation, and shell-init RPC updates once the target SDK session wrapper is no longer `'active'` or has been disposed, including inside queued sequencer callbacks and after async file preparation.
  - Scope `isSessionClosed(session)` to the specific `CopilotSession` being configured and clear `_wrapper` on teardown so telemetry-revocation relaunches still apply launch sandbox configuration to replacement SDK sessions.

## Validation

## Summary

Sessions started with the standalone Copilot CLI on a Remote-SSH host are cataloged by the agent host, but never appear in VS Code's Sessions view. The reverse direction works: sessions started in VS Code appear in the CLI's Sessions tab.

I'd like two things:

1. CLI sessions run inside the agent host, so they persist the same way VS Code sessions do.
2. Resume anywhere, in the CLI or in VS Code, one writer at a time, as web-based agent UIs allow.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.144.0 (stable) over Remote-SSH to a Linux host
- Copilot CLI 1.0.105, launched via `gh copilot`
- Agent host running on the remote (`code ... agent host`)

## Observations

On the remote, `~/.vscode-server/data/agentSessionData/<id>/session.db` has a `session_metadata` table.

- Across about 1,480 records, the 162 started from VS Code (`vscode.session.initiator` is `vscode` or `vscode-editor-window`) all have `defaultChatProviderData` with an `sdkSessionId`.
- CLI-started sessions (`vscode.session.initiator = {"name":"github/cli"}`) have a record but no `defaultChatProviderData`. The CLI's own `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/` directory is the only place the conversation lives, and the CLI process owns it.
- The record is created on the first turn.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a VS Code Remote-SSH terminal, start `copilot` in the open workspace folder.
2. Run `/ide`, then send a prompt.
3. Open the Sessions view in VS Code.

## Actual

The session isn't listed. Its `agentSessionData` entry has no chat-provider binding, and the session ends with the CLI process rather than persisting in the agent host.

## Expected

A CLI-started session is hosted by the agent host and bound like any other. It can be opened from VS Code or resumed from the CLI, with a single-writer rule while another client is attached.

## Other notes

- VS Code terminals put a `copilot-shim` on `PATH`. With only `gh copilot` installed, `gh copilot` then finds the shim and offers to install the CLI instead of using the existing binary.

title: Local Hooks list stays empty for a hooks-only plugin until another plugin refreshes discovery

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

body:
Testing #343747

## Summary

With only an enabled SDK-installed hooks-only plugin, **Customizations (Local) > Hooks** initially shows no hooks. Installing a mixed-contribution plugin from the same marketplace makes both plugins' hooks appear. Removing the mixed plugin leaves the original hooks-only plugin's two hooks visible.

The observed Local inventory transition is **0 -> 4 -> 2**, without changing hook settings.

## Environment

- Code OSS Dev 1.145.0, Windows 11 x64, main `f9ba073c04dd7f0d2b8ec4e9aa49dfdcd4d9c3ca`
- Node.js 24.22.1
- Fresh isolated authenticated profile, empty workspace outside the fixture repository, and aligned disposable `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, and `COPILOT_HOME`
- Fixture repository: https://github.com/aeschli/vscode-agent-plugin-test-fixtures at `edb89300e2ee1ec26265eab286e1c97cfb624f61`
- Installation through the **Copilot** harness's SDK marketplace; the failing inventory surface is the **Local** harness, not a remote Agent Host

## Repro steps

1. Start the build above with a fresh profile and no installed test plugins. Use a separate, trusted disposable workspace. Keep the normal user/Copilot home untouched.
2. Verify **Chat: Use Hooks** (`chat.useHooks`) is enabled. In the controlled run it was checked in both User and Workspace settings, editable, and unchanged throughout. `chat.useClaudeHooks` was at its default `false`; these fixtures use Copilot-format `hooks.json`.
3. Select the **Copilot** harness. Open **Customizations > Plugins > Configure Marketplaces**, add `aeschli/vscode-agent-plugin-test-fixtures`, and browse catalog `vscode-agent-plugin-fixtures`.
4. Install **only `fixture-hooks-only`**.
5. Select the **Local** harness by its visible picker label. Open **Customizations > Plugins** and verify `fixture-hooks-only` is **Enabled**, its profile switch is checked, and its details report **2 hooks**.
6. Open **Hooks**. Leave the search empty. The page shows **User 0 / Workspace 0**, with no plugin hook rows. The recorded view was still empty approximately **40 seconds** after opening it.
7. Return to Copilot's marketplace and additionally install **`fixture-mixed`** from the same catalog. Do not change settings or disable the hooks-only plugin.
8. Return to **Customizations (Local) > Hooks**. Now all **four** rows appear: `sessionStart` and `userPromptSubmitted` for each plugin.
9. Uninstall **only `fixture-mixed`** through Copilot Browse, then return to Local Hooks. The two **`fixture-hooks-only`** rows remain visible.

## Expected

The enabled hooks-only plugin's two hooks appear at step 6, without installing another plugin to refresh the inventory.

## Actual

The initial list is empty. Adding the mixed plugin makes the previously missing hooks-only entries visible, and they remain visible after the mixed plugin is removed.

## Controls and scope

- The modal title explicitly showed **Local** for each inventory observation; this was not inferred from an attempted harness switch.
- The hooks-only plugin was enabled before the empty view. Both plugins were enabled in the positive control.
- **Developer: Policy Diagnostics** showed an inactive account gate, zero managed-setting keys, and **0 applied policies**. The managed-hooks-only and strict-plugin-only policies were not applied. No policy was changed or bypassed.
- The controlled workspace was trusted via the process-scoped `--disable-workspace-trust` launch flag.
- The private profile had only the launcher's title/simple-dialog settings; there were no workspace settings, and the settings hash did not change.
- No model-backed Local runtime was tested: **zero SDK user messages/tool executions**, no fixture hook marker file, and no manual MCP Start. This report is about **Local UI inventory/refresh**, not a claim that Local hooks failed to execute.
- The sequence is consistent with initialization/refresh behavior, but the code cause and whether other actions can trigger recovery have not been established.

Related but distinct: #343572 and #330114 concern Copilot Agent Host hook publication. This report concerns the controlled **Local** inventory transition above.
